fields.hint: My very long bill curves down toward the mud.

fields.summary: The Gadwall is a duck with plain feathers. The grey male has a black rear end and a small white patch on the wing.
fields.behaviour: It mostly eats water plants taken near the surface. It can also pick up plants brought up by other birds.
fields.why_here: Ponds, marshes and shallow lakes give it water plants and sheltered shores.
fields.migration: It is present all year in some French regions. Migrants and winter visitors add to the numbers depending on the season.
fields.by_ear: The male gives short, low calls. The female quacks like other ducks.
fields.confusions: The female looks like a female Mallard. The white patch on the wing helps you recognize the Gadwall.
fields.anecdote: Up close, the male's grey feathers show fine wavy lines.
fields.hint: My plain grey hides fine wavy lines and a white wing patch.

fields.summary: The Water Rail is a shy marsh bird. Its long red bill sticks out of a blue-grey face, and its sides are striped.
fields.behaviour: It walks through thick plants to take small animals and seeds. It slips between the stems with ease.
fields.why_here: Reedbeds, ditches and marsh edges give it hidden paths by the water.
fields.migration: It is present all year in some regions of France. Migrant birds also join French marshes in autumn and winter.
fields.by_ear: It gives high, squealing cries that can sound like a little pig. These calls give away its presence in the reeds.
fields.confusions: The Common Moorhen is bigger and has a short bill. The Water Rail has a clearly long, red bill.
fields.anecdote: Its narrow body helps it move through very tight plants.
fields.hint: A little-pig squeal comes from the reeds where I hide.

fields.summary: The Stock Dove is a shy grey pigeon with a slightly shimmering neck. It looks for holes to build its nest.
fields.behaviour: It mostly eats seeds, often on the ground in fields. It can feed in groups outside the breeding season.
fields.why_here: Old hollow trees give it nesting places. Woods close to open land offer both shelter and food.
fields.migration: You can see it all year in France. Some populations move, and birds from elsewhere pass through or spend the winter here.
fields.by_ear: Its song is a low, repeated, fairly dull coo. It does not carry as far as the Common Wood Pigeon's.
fields.confusions: The Common Wood Pigeon has white marks on the wings and neck. The Stock Dove does not have these big white patches.
fields.anecdote: It can use a hole dug earlier by a big woodpecker.
fields.hint: My nest hides in a hole in an old tree.

fields.summary: The Common Gull is a modest-sized gull with a light grey back. The adult has a fairly thin bill and yellow-green legs.
fields.behaviour: It eats fish, worms and other small animals. It can look for food in fields, on beaches or on the water's surface.
fields.why_here: Coasts, river mouths, lakes and farmland give it places to feed and rest.
fields.migration: It is most numerous in France in the cold season. A few birds nest in the country, so you can see it at different times.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are fairly high and sad-sounding for a gull. Calls alone do not always tell it apart.
fields.confusions: The European Herring Gull is bigger and has a heavier bill. The Common Gull looks more delicate, with a rounder head.
fields.anecdote: It can take advantage of a plow's work to find small animals in the soil.
fields.hint: My thin bill goes with yellow-green legs.

fields.summary: The Ring Ouzel looks like a dark blackbird with a white crescent on its chest. It is often tied to hills and mountains.
fields.behaviour: It looks for worms and insects on the ground. It also eats berries, especially outside the breeding season.
fields.why_here: Grassy slopes, heaths and mountain edges give it food and shelter. Migrants can stop at lower heights.
fields.migration: It nests in the French mountains and also crosses the country during migration. In winter, many go to regions further south.
fields.by_ear: Its song has short, repeated patterns, less varied than the Common Blackbird's. Its alarm calls are dry.
fields.confusions: The Common Blackbird does not have the wide white crescent on its chest. In young birds, this mark can be less clear.
fields.anecdote: You can meet it far from the mountains when it stops during migration.
fields.hint: A white crescent brightens my dark chest in the mountains.

fields.summary: The Wood Warbler is a small woodland bird with a greenish back and a white belly. Its face and throat are tinted yellow.
fields.behaviour: It catches small insects in the leaves. It sings from a branch and can make short singing flights.
fields.why_here: Forests with tall trees and a fairly open undergrowth suit it. Its nest is on the ground, well hidden.
fields.migration: It is a migrant: it comes back to France in spring and leaves after breeding to spend the winter in Africa.
fields.by_ear: Its song starts with spaced-out notes, then speeds up into a trill. It also gives runs of sad-sounding whistles.
fields.confusions: The Willow Warbler has a more melodious song that goes down. The Wood Warbler is mostly known by its phrase that speeds up.
fields.anecdote: Although it lives in the leaves, it builds its nest on the ground.
fields.hint: My song speeds up until it trembles under tall trees.

fields.summary: The Eurasian Wryneck is a small bird with brown and grey feathers that look like bark. Although it is a woodpecker relative, its bill stays fairly thin.
fields.behaviour: It mostly looks for ants and their larvae. Its tongue lets it scoop them up from their tunnels.
fields.why_here: Orchards, edges and countryside with old trees give it holes to nest in and places to look for ants.
fields.migration: You see it mostly in the warm season in France and during migration. Most leave to spend the winter further south.
fields.by_ear: Its song is a run of repeated, nasal, fairly loud notes. From far away, it can remind you of some birds of prey.
fields.confusions: Its feathers are very different from the black and white woodpeckers. Sitting still against the bark, it is mostly hard to spot.
fields.anecdote: When it feels threatened, it can twist its neck in surprising ways.
fields.hint: I catch ants with my sticky tongue.

fields.summary: The Short-eared Owl is a night bird of prey of open country. Its yellow eyes are ringed with dark, and its small ear tufts often stay hard to see.
fields.behaviour: It flies low to look mostly for small mammals. It also hunts by day, especially when food is needed for the chicks.
fields.why_here: Meadows, marshes and heaths give it hunting grounds. Its nest is hidden in plants on the ground.
fields.migration: You can see it in France in different seasons. Birds move a lot depending on food, and local breeding changes from year to year.
fields.by_ear: It is often quiet. During displays, you can hear low calls and wing claps.
fields.confusions: The Long-eared Owl has orange eyes and longer ear tufts. The Short-eared Owl is more often seen hunting over open ground.
fields.anecdote: It can hunt in broad daylight, despite its image as a night bird.
fields.hint: My yellow eyes watch the meadows even in broad daylight.

fields.summary: The Curlew Sandpiper is a small shorebird with a long, curved bill. Its breeding plumage turns mostly rusty.
fields.behaviour: It probes the mud and pecks at small animals. It often mixes with other shorebirds during stops.
fields.why_here: Mudflats, lagoons and shallow ponds give it stops to rebuild its energy.
fields.migration: It crosses France during migration, mostly at the end of summer. Seeing it in summer does not mean it nests in the country.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are short and thin. In a flock, visual details are often more useful to identify it.
fields.confusions: The Dunlin usually has a shorter bill and a dark center to its rump. The Curlew Sandpiper shows a white rump in flight.
fields.anecdote: Its rusty breeding feathers give way to much paler colors in winter.
fields.hint: A white rump shows when I take off.

fields.summary: The European Nightjar is a night bird with bark-colored feathers. By day it rests almost motionless and blends into its surroundings.
fields.behaviour: It catches insects in flight, mostly as night falls. Its wide throat opens up to snap up its prey.
fields.why_here: Heaths, clearings and open woods give it hunting grounds. It lays its eggs straight on the ground.
fields.migration: It comes back to France in the warm season and flies off to Africa after breeding.
fields.by_ear: The male makes a long, vibrating purr, fairly steady. Wing claps can go with displays.
fields.confusions: In night flight, it can remind you of a bat. Its long wings and tail still show the shape of a bird.
fields.anecdote: Its bill looks tiny when closed, but its mouth opens very wide to hunt.
fields.hint: My vibrating purr rises from the heath at dusk.

fields.summary: The Water Pipit is a small mountain bird in summer. Its feathers change from a pinker chest in spring to more streaky tones in winter.
fields.behaviour: It walks on the ground to catch insects and other small prey. The male can sing in flight over his territory.
fields.why_here: It nests in mountain grasslands. At other times, it also visits wet meadows and water edges in the lowlands.
fields.migration: Present all year in France, it often changes height or region. Winter sites are usually lower than breeding sites.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are short and high. Its song is mostly heard in mountain territories.
fields.confusions: The Rock Pipit lives mostly on rocky coasts and often looks darker. In winter, pipits need careful watching.
fields.anecdote: The same bird can spend summer in the mountains and winter near a lowland marsh.
fields.hint: I come down from mountain meadows to winter marshes.

fields.summary: The Common Crane is a big grey bird with long legs and a long neck. Its migrating flocks can be heard from very far away.
fields.behaviour: It feeds on the ground on seeds, shoots and small animals. Groups often go to a wetland to sleep.
fields.why_here: Fields give it food. Big marshes and shallow water give it places to rest.
fields.migration: France welcomes big migrations and winter visitors. A few birds also nest in the country, but the big gatherings are mostly seasonal.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are powerful, rolling and trumpet-like. They often let you find a flock before you see it.
fields.confusions: The Grey Heron folds its neck in flight. The Common Crane flies with its neck stretched out and its legs sticking out behind.
fields.anecdote: The calls keep the birds of a traveling group in touch.
fields.hint: My trumpeting calls announce a big V-shaped flight.

fields.summary: The Tawny Pipit is a small beige bird of dry ground. Its lightly streaked feathers and long legs give it a slender look.
fields.behaviour: It runs or walks on the ground to look for insects. Sometimes it uses a small high spot as a song post.
fields.why_here: Dry heaths, dunes, sparse grass and stony ground give it open spaces to feed and nest on the ground.
fields.migration: It is a migrant: it stays in France in the warm season, then goes to Africa for the winter.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are short and clear. The song is made of fairly simple, repeated patterns.
fields.confusions: The Meadow Pipit is more clearly streaked on the chest. The adult Tawny Pipit looks plainer and likes dry, bare ground.
fields.anecdote: Its pale feathers make it hard to see on sandy ground.
fields.hint: My beige feathers blend in among stones and sand.

fields.summary: The Garganey is a small duck. The male has a wide white eyebrow crossing his brown head.
fields.behaviour: It takes small prey and plants in shallow water. It likes to hide among marsh plants.
fields.why_here: Marshes, flooded meadows and shallow ponds give it food and shelter for nesting.
fields.migration: It comes back to France in spring, breeds here in a few places, then leaves for Africa. It is mostly here in the warm season.
fields.by_ear: The male makes a dry, crackling sound, very different from a quack. The female's calls are quieter.
fields.confusions: The male Green-winged Teal has a green band on his head. The male Garganey has a wide white eyebrow.
fields.anecdote: Its call can remind you of the dry click of a little machine.
fields.hint: My big white eyebrow crosses a brown head.

fields.summary: The Black-necked Grebe is a small diving bird. In breeding plumage, it has golden tufts behind its red eyes.
fields.behaviour: It dives to catch small water animals. It often nests in groups and builds a floating nest.
fields.why_here: Ponds rich in plants host its breeding. In winter, it also uses big lakes and lagoons.
fields.migration: You can see it all year in France, but it changes sites with the season. Birds from elsewhere also join the winter homes.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are fairly thin, sometimes whistled or trembling. You hear them mostly near breeding groups.
fields.confusions: The Horned Grebe in winter has a head with a more clearly contrasting pattern. The Black-necked Grebe has a thin, slightly upturned bill.
fields.anecdote: The nest rests on a heap of plants held to the water plants.
fields.hint: Golden fans open behind my red eyes in summer.

fields.summary: The Lesser Whitethroat is a small, shy bird with a white throat. Its grey head has darker cheeks.
fields.behaviour: It looks for insects in branches and bushes. It also eats small fruits, depending on the season.
fields.why_here: Thick hedges, thickets and edges give it shelter, food and places to hold its nest.
fields.migration: It is a migrant: it comes back to France in the warm season and leaves for winter homes further south.
fields.by_ear: Its song has a run of dry, repeated notes that seems to rattle from the bush.
fields.confusions: The Common Whitethroat shows more rust on the wings. The Lesser Whitethroat has a greyer head and darker cheeks.
fields.anecdote: It can stay completely hidden in a bush while still singing a clear song.
fields.hint: I sing dry, repeated notes from deep in the bush.

fields.summary: The Alpine Swift is a big bird with sickle-shaped wings. A brown band separates its white belly from its pale throat.
fields.behaviour: It catches insects in flight and spends a lot of time in the air. It goes to a hole to nest.
fields.why_here: Cliffs and tall buildings give it cracks for the nest. The air around gives the insects it chases.
fields.migration: It comes back to France in the warm season and goes to spend the winter in Africa. The dates it is here vary by region.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are fast, loud trills, often heard when several birds circle near their colony.
fields.confusions: The Common Swift is smaller and almost all dark. The white belly of the Alpine Swift shows in good light.
fields.anecdote: It also picks up, in flight, small bits carried by the air for its nest.

fields.summary: The Red Crossbill is a conifer bird with an amazing bill: its two tips cross over. The male is often red and the female greenish.
fields.behaviour: It pries open the scales of cones with its bill to reach the seeds. It moves among branches, helping itself with its feet.
fields.why_here: Conifer forests give it the cones it feeds on. It looks for places where seeds are available.
fields.migration: You can see it all year in France, but groups move depending on cone crops. Unusual arrivals can happen some years.
fields.by_ear: Its contact calls are dry and metallic, often repeated in flight. Their variety does not always make detailed identification easy.
fields.confusions: Other crossbills look like it. The bill shape, the wings and the calls must then be checked carefully.
fields.anecdote: It can breed in the middle of winter when cones give enough food.

fields.summary: The Eurasian Goshawk is a powerful forest bird of prey. Its rounded wings and long tail help it steer between trees.
fields.behaviour: It catches birds and mammals in quick attacks. It uses the cover of trees to get close to its prey.
fields.why_here: Woods give it nest sites and hiding places. Nearby edges and open spaces add to its hunting ground.
fields.migration: It is usually present all year in the French regions where it nests. Young birds can scatter far from where they were born.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are runs of loud, dry notes, mostly heard near the nest.
fields.confusions: The Eurasian Sparrowhawk is usually smaller and slimmer. The adult Eurasian Goshawk has a sturdy head with a pale eyebrow.
fields.anecdote: The female is much bigger than the male.
fields.hint: My rounded wings guide my chases between the trees.

fields.summary: The Woodlark is a small brown bird with a pale eyebrow. Its eyebrows seem to meet behind the head, and its tail is short.
fields.behaviour: It walks on the ground to look for seeds and insects. It sings in flight, but also from a tree or a bush.
fields.why_here: Heaths, clearings and open hillsides dotted with trees give it feeding areas and places for a ground nest.
fields.migration: It is present all year in some French regions. Other birds move and spend the cold season further south.
fields.by_ear: Its song is soft, flute-like and melodious, with repeated falling patterns. It can also ring out at night.
fields.confusions: The Eurasian Skylark has a longer tail and a more non-stop song. The strong eyebrow and short tail help you know the Woodlark.
fields.anecdote: It can sing from a branch, unlike the image of a lark always above the fields.
fields.hint: My short tail goes with a soft song of falling notes.

fields.summary: The Grey Plover is a fairly sturdy shorebird. Its back looks grey and speckled, and its belly turns black in breeding plumage.
fields.behaviour: It alternates runs and pauses to take prey from the mud. It waits for the movement of a small animal to give it away.
fields.why_here: Mudflats and open beaches give it huge feeding areas uncovered at low tide.
fields.migration: You find it on French coasts mostly during migration and in winter. Some birds also stay in other seasons without breeding here.
fields.by_ear: Its call is a clear, sad whistle, often made of several notes.
fields.confusions: The European Golden Plover does not have black armpits. You can see this dark patch when the Grey Plover lifts its wings or takes off.
fields.anecdote: A small black patch under each wing lets you recognize it even when its feathers change.
fields.hint: My black armpits show when I lift my wings.

fields.summary: The Common Grasshopper Warbler is a small streaky brown bird, often invisible in the grass. Its non-stop song sounds more like an insect than a bird.
fields.behaviour: It slips along near the ground to look for insects. It often stays hidden in thick plants.
fields.why_here: Grassy wasteland, wet meadows and low thickets give it dense cover to eat and nest.
fields.migration: It is a migrant: it comes back to France in spring and leaves after breeding to spend the winter in Africa.
fields.by_ear: Its song is a long, steady buzz. The sound seems to get louder or softer when the bird turns its head.
fields.confusions: Insects can make a similar noise. To tell close birds apart, you also need to think about the habitat and the rhythm.
fields.anecdote: It can sing for a long time without leaving its hiding place.
fields.hint: I stay hidden in the grass and sing for a long time.

fields.summary: The White-throated Dipper is a dark brown bird with a white chest. It lives by fast-running water and can dive to find food.
fields.behaviour: It walks, swims and dives to take small water animals. Sitting on a stone, it often bobs its body.
fields.why_here: Streams and rivers with running water give it prey. Rocks, banks and structures can hold its nest.
fields.migration: It is usually present all year in the French regions where it lives. Some birds change area when conditions become hard.
fields.by_ear: Its song mixes clear notes and rougher sounds. It can still be heard over the noise of the current.
fields.confusions: Its white chest and its dives in rivers set it apart from blackbirds or small birds on the banks.
fields.anecdote: It can look for prey under water, using its wings to hold itself against the current.
fields.hint: I walk, swim and dive in the fast water of the stream.

fields.summary: The Ruddy Turnstone is a stocky shore bird with a short bill. It searches through the debris left by the sea.
fields.behaviour: It flips small objects with its bill to dislodge the animals hidden below. It walks among pebbles, seaweed and shells.
fields.why_here: Rocky coasts, pebble beaches and harbor structures give it many hiding places to explore.
fields.migration: You find it in France mostly during migration and in winter. Some birds stay on the coasts in summer without nesting.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are dry and quick, with a slightly rolling sound. They often go with the movements of a group.
fields.confusions: Its stocky shape and short bill set it apart from the redshanks and greenshanks. In flight, its back and wings show a very contrasting white pattern.
fields.anecdote: It does not only turn over stones: seaweed and small debris can also hide a meal.
fields.hint: I search the pebbles, seaweed and shells by the sea.

fields.summary: Montagu's Harrier is a slim bird of prey with long wings. The grey male has a black bar on each wing.
fields.behaviour: It hunts by flying low over grass and crops. It catches small mammals, birds and big insects.
fields.why_here: Open plains, meadows and crops give it prey. Its nest is hidden on the ground in fairly tall plants.
fields.migration: It comes back to France in spring to breed and leaves for Africa after the warm season.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are mostly heard near the nest and during exchanges between adults. It is often silent when hunting.
fields.confusions: The male Hen Harrier is sturdier and has no black bar on the wing. Females need careful watching.
fields.anecdote: In crop fields, the nest may still be in use when the harvest comes.
fields.hint: A black bar crosses each of my long grey wings.

fields.summary: The Hooded Crow has a grey coat on its body. Its head, wings and tail stay black.
fields.behaviour: It eats varied food, from seeds to small animals and leftovers. It often looks for food on the ground.
fields.why_here: It visits open country with trees, coasts and built-up areas. Trees give it places for the nest.
fields.migration: For France, it is mostly present all year in Corsica. On the French mainland, sightings are much more local or occasional.
fields.by_ear: Its caws are close to those of the Carrion Crow. Feathers are usually more useful than the voice to tell them apart.
fields.confusions: The Carrion Crow is all dark. Birds in between exist in places where the two breed together.
fields.anecdote: It can breed with the Carrion Crow where their populations meet.
fields.hint: I wear a grey coat with black wings.

fields.summary: The Eurasian Whimbrel is a shorebird with a bill that curves downward. Its head has dark stripes split by a paler line.
fields.behaviour: It catches small animals on mud and coasts. Depending on the place, it can also eat berries.
fields.why_here: Mudflats, river mouths and rocky shores give it places to rest and feed during its travels.
fields.migration: You see it in France mainly during spring migration and in late summer. Some birds can also spend the winter on the coast.
fields.by_ear: Its call is a quick run of whistled notes, often repeated when it takes off.
fields.confusions: The Eurasian Curlew is usually bigger and has a longer bill. The Eurasian Whimbrel shows clearer stripes on the head.
fields.anecdote: Its curved bill lets it grab prey in hard-to-reach places.
fields.hint: My striped head goes with a curved bill and quick calls.

fields.summary: The Woodchat Shrike is a small hunter that hunts from a perch. The adult has a rusty cap above a dark mask.
fields.behaviour: It watches from a branch or a wire, then catches big insects. Now and then it also takes small animals with a backbone.
fields.why_here: Orchards, pastures and open country dotted with trees give it lookout posts and hunting grounds.
fields.migration: It comes back to France in the warm season, mostly in the south. Then it leaves for the winter in Africa.
fields.by_ear: Its song mixes varied notes and sometimes imitations. Its calls are dry and easier to notice.
fields.confusions: The male Red-backed Shrike has a grey head and a rusty back. The adult Woodchat Shrike has the rust on top of its head.
fields.anecdote: Like other shrikes, it can pin prey on thorns.
fields.hint: My rusty cap sits above a dark mask at my lookout post.

fields.summary: The Bluethroat is a small wetland bird. The male has a blue throat, sometimes with a pale or rusty spot.
fields.behaviour: It looks for insects and small prey near the ground. It sometimes steps out into the open, then quickly goes back to protective plants.
fields.why_here: Reedbeds, marshes and wet thickets give it shelter. Bare patches of ground close by make it easier to find food.
fields.migration: It nests in a few places in France and also crosses the country during migration. Most birds spend the winter further south.
fields.by_ear: Its song is varied, with whistled phrases and sounds copied from other birds. The male often sings from a visible perch.
fields.confusions: The female is much less colorful than the male. The rusty base of the tail and the pale eyebrow can help you recognize her.
fields.anecdote: The patterns on the throat differ between populations and with the plumage.
fields.hint: I sing from a visible perch near the reeds.

fields.summary: The Great Grey Shrike is a grey, white and black bird with a dark mask. It watches open country from a high perch.
fields.behaviour: It catches big insects and small animals with a backbone. It can pin some prey on a thorn or barbed wire.
fields.why_here: Meadows, heaths and countryside with hedges give it hunting grounds and lookout posts.
fields.migration: It is present all year in some regions of France. Movements and arrivals of birds from the north change where it lives in winter.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are often dry and rasping. Its quieter song can include imitations.
fields.confusions: The Southern Grey Shrike looks like it and needs careful watching. The region, the proportions and the shades of the feathers must be considered together.
fields.anecdote: Prey pinned on points can serve as a food store.
fields.hint: My dark mask dominates the meadows from a high perch.

fields.summary: The Black-winged Stilt is a black and white bird with extremely long pink legs. Its black bill is thin and straight.
fields.behaviour: It walks in shallow water to peck at small animals. Its long legs let it explore different water depths.
fields.why_here: Marshes, lagoons and shallow pools give it food and little islands for the nest.
fields.migration: You find it in France mostly in the warm season. Many birds migrate, while some stay for the winter in good regions.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are high, short and repeated. They become insistent when an intruder comes near the nest area.
fields.confusions: The Pied Avocet has a clearly upturned bill and blue-grey legs. The Black-winged Stilt has a straight bill and pink legs.
fields.anecdote: Its legs stick out far past the tail when it flies.
fields.hint: My very long pink legs wade across the marsh.

fields.summary: The Purple Heron is a big, slender heron in rusty and dark colors. Its long striped neck blends in among the reeds.
fields.behaviour: It watches for fish and other small animals in wet plants. It often moves slowly and carefully.
fields.why_here: Big reedbeds give it hiding places and nest sites. Nearby ditches and waters are used for hunting.
fields.migration: It comes back to France in spring and leaves after breeding for Africa, where it spends the winter.
fields.by_ear: Its flight calls are rough. In the reeds, it often stays silent and hard to spot.
fields.confusions: The Grey Heron is greyer and bulkier. The Purple Heron has a thinner neck with lots of rusty and dark marks.
fields.anecdote: When it stretches its neck among the reeds, its stripes make its camouflage even better.
fields.hint: My long rusty, striped neck blends in with the reeds.

fields.summary: The Short-toed Snake Eagle is a big bird of prey with a pale underside. Its wide head and big eyes go with a hunt specialized in reptiles.
fields.behaviour: It watches the ground from the sky or a perch, then drops down to grab mostly snakes. It can stay briefly in place in the wind.
fields.why_here: Open country rich in reptiles gives it food. Nearby woods provide trees to nest in.
fields.migration: It comes back to France in spring and leaves for Africa after the warm season.
fields.by_ear: It sometimes gives whistled calls, but it is often silent when it hunts.
fields.confusions: The Common Buzzard can also have a pale underside. The Short-toed Snake Eagle looks bigger, with a big head and long, wide wings.
fields.anecdote: It can swallow a snake starting with the head.
fields.hint: I hover briefly in the wind over open land.

fields.summary: The Red-crested Pochard is a duck whose male has a big orange head and a red bill. The female has softer brown tones.
fields.behaviour: It mostly eats water plants. It can feed at the surface, tip forward or dive.
fields.why_here: Lakes and ponds rich in water plants give it food. Sheltered shores hold the nests.
fields.migration: You can see it all year in some regions of France. Seasonal movements change where the groups gather on the lakes.
fields.by_ear: It is usually fairly quiet. The sounds it makes when meeting others are less useful than its feathers for identifying it.
fields.confusions: The male Common Pochard has a smaller head and a dark bill. The male Red-crested Pochard stands out with its bright red bill.
fields.anecdote: The male can offer food to the female during courtship.
fields.hint: During courtship, I offer food to my mate.

fields.summary: The Red-breasted Merganser is a diving duck with a long, thin bill. Its shaggy crest gives its head a special shape.
fields.behaviour: It dives to chase fish. Little points on the edges of its bill help it hold slippery prey.
fields.why_here: Coastal waters, river mouths and big lakes give it fishing grounds.
fields.migration: In France, you find it mostly in the cold season and during migration, especially on the coast. It breeds mainly further north.
fields.by_ear: It is often quiet in winter. Its sounds are usually less useful than its shape and feathers for recognizing it.
fields.confusions: The female Goosander has a sharper split between the rusty head and the pale neck. The Red-breasted Merganser's looks more finely billed and shaggy.
fields.anecdote: Its bill holds fish thanks to little points aimed backward.
fields.hint: My ruffled crest goes with a thin fisher's bill.

fields.summary: The Eurasian Spoonbill is a big white bird with a flat bill that is wider at the tip. It looks for food by sweeping the water with its head.
fields.behaviour: It walks in shallow water with its bill a little open and swings it from side to side to catch small prey.
fields.why_here: Marshes, river mouths and lagoons give it shallow water to hunt in. It nests in colonies on supports that suit the site.
fields.migration: It nests in France and also passes through during migration. Some birds spend the winter in the country, while others go further south.
fields.by_ear: Adults are usually not very noisy. Young birds are louder when they beg for food.
fields.confusions: Egrets have a pointed bill. The Eurasian Spoonbill has a bill that is wide at the tip and flies with its neck stretched out.
fields.anecdote: The shape of its bill lets it search by touch in cloudy water.
fields.hint: My wide bill sweeps the water from side to side.

fields.summary: The Ortolan Bunting is a small bird of open countryside. The male has a greenish-grey head, a yellow throat and a rusty belly.
fields.behaviour: It looks for seeds and small animals on the ground. During breeding, insects are part of the food brought to the chicks.
fields.why_here: Varied crops, hillsides and open spaces with trees or bushes give it food and song posts.
fields.migration: It comes back to France in the warm season and leaves for Africa for the winter. Its breeding in France is mostly local.
fields.by_ear: Its song is a short phrase of repeated notes, ending with a different, longer note.
fields.confusions: The male Yellowhammer has a much yellower head. The Ortolan Bunting has a pale ring around the eye and a more rusty belly.
fields.anecdote: It can sing from a lone tree while going to look for food on the ground.
fields.hint: My yellow throat contrasts with a rusty belly.

fields.summary: The Pied Avocet is a black and white bird with long blue-grey legs. Its thin bill curves clearly upward.
fields.behaviour: It sweeps the water with its bill to catch small prey. It can also peck or swim.
fields.why_here: Lagoons, salt marshes and mudflats give it shallow water and bare islets for nesting.
fields.migration: It is present all year in some regions of France. Birds can still migrate or change sites between breeding and winter.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are loud, short and flute-like. Near a colony, the birds can sound the alarm noisily.
fields.confusions: The Black-winged Stilt has pink legs and a straight bill. The Pied Avocet has blue-grey legs and an upturned bill.
fields.anecdote: Its curved bill searches the water with side-to-side movements.
fields.hint: My bill curves up toward the sky over the mud.

fields.summary: The Great Reed Warbler is a big brown bird of the reeds. Its strong bill goes with a powerful, rasping voice.
fields.behaviour: It grabs insects and other small prey among the stems. It grips the reeds firmly to move around or sing.
fields.why_here: Tall reedbeds by the water give it song posts and supports for its nest.
fields.migration: It is a migrant: it comes back to France in spring and goes to Africa after breeding.
fields.by_ear: Its song is loud, rhythmic and grating, with groups of repeated sounds. It carries far over the marsh.
fields.confusions: The Eurasian Reed Warbler is smaller and has a thinner bill. The voice of the Great Reed Warbler is more powerful and lower.
fields.anecdote: Its nest hangs between several reed stems.
fields.hint: I hang my nest between several tall stems.

fields.summary: The Sanderling is a small beach bird, often very pale in winter. It runs at the edge of the waves on its black legs.
fields.behaviour: It follows the water as it pulls back to peck at small prey in the sand. It quickly runs back when a new wave comes.
fields.why_here: Sandy beaches give it food brought or uncovered by the sea. It also uses other shores during its travels.
fields.migration: You can see it on French coasts mainly during migration and in winter. A few birds can stay in summer without breeding here.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are short and thin. The back-and-forth at the edge of the waves is often a clearer clue than the voice.
fields.confusions: The Dunlin has a longer, slightly curved bill. In winter, the Sanderling often looks clearly whiter.
fields.anecdote: It has no back-pointing toe, unlike many other small shorebirds.
fields.hint: I run behind the waves and flee when they come back.

fields.summary: The Jack Snipe is a very small marsh bird with streaky brown feathers. It often stays still and hidden until the last moment.
fields.behaviour: It looks for small animals in soaked ground. While feeding, it can bob its whole body regularly.
fields.why_here: Waterlogged meadows, marshes and wet edges rich in low plants give it shelter and food.
fields.migration: It comes to France mostly in the cold season and during migration. It goes to regions further north to breed.
fields.by_ear: It is usually silent when met on its wintering grounds. Its name does not mean it cannot hear.
fields.confusions: The Common Snipe is bigger and has a proportionally longer bill. It often flies up from farther away.
fields.anecdote: Its camouflage and stillness let it go unnoticed a few steps away.
fields.hint: I stay still in wet grass until the last moment.

fields.summary: The Spotted Redshank is a slender bird with long legs. Its feathers change a lot, turning almost black in the breeding season.
fields.behaviour: It takes small animals in shallow water. It can wade fairly deep and sometimes swims while looking for food.
fields.why_here: Marshes, lagoons and mudflats give it places to feed and rest.
fields.migration: It crosses France during migration and some birds spend the winter here. It breeds in regions further north.
fields.by_ear: Its call is clear and whistled, often made of two notes close together.
fields.confusions: The Common Redshank has a shorter bill and a wide white band on the wings in flight. The Spotted Redshank does not have this band.
fields.anecdote: The same bird can look almost black in summer and very pale in winter.
fields.hint: Almost black in summer, I turn much paler in winter.

fields.summary: The Glossy Ibis is a dark bird with a long curved bill. In good light, its feathers show green and coppery shine.
fields.behaviour: It probes wet ground and shallow water to take small animals. It often feeds in groups.
fields.why_here: Marshes, flooded meadows and rice fields give it food. It nests in colonies in sheltered wet places.
fields.migration: It nests in France and can be seen all year in some regions. Movements and scattering change where it is found locally.
fields.by_ear: It is often silent while feeding. Rough sounds can be heard when birds meet at the colony.
fields.confusions: The Eurasian Curlew has streaky brown feathers and a different shape. The Glossy Ibis looks more evenly dark with long legs.
fields.anecdote: Its feathers can look black in the shade and turn colorful when the sun lights them.
fields.hint: I feed in groups, probing wet ground.

fields.summary: The Black Stork is a big dark bird with a white belly. The adult has a red bill and red legs.
fields.behaviour: It looks for fish and other small prey in shallow water. It is usually shyer than the White Stork.
fields.why_here: Big forests give it trees to nest in. Nearby streams, pools and wet meadows are used for feeding.
fields.migration: You see it in France mostly in the warm season and during migration. Most leave for the south, although a few birds may spend the winter.
fields.by_ear: It is often silent. Sounds near the nest are less useful for finding it than watching from a distance.
fields.confusions: The White Stork has a mostly white body. The Black Stork keeps a dark neck, chest and back.
fields.anecdote: It can hide its big nest in a tree deep in a forest.
fields.hint: I hide my big nest in a tree deep in a forest.

fields.summary: The Black-tailed Godwit is a big shorebird with a long, almost straight bill. In flight, it shows a black tail and a white rump.
fields.behaviour: It probes mud and wet ground to find small animals. It can also eat plant food.
fields.why_here: Wet meadows, marshes and mudflats give it food and rest. Suitable meadows host the few French nesters.
fields.migration: It crosses France and spends the winter here, while one population nests in a few places. Birds seen in different seasons can come from different places.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are loud and nasal. You hear them especially when birds take off or meet.
fields.confusions: The Bar-tailed Godwit often has a more upturned bill and a barred tail. The Black-tailed Godwit also shows a clear white band on the wing in flight.
fields.anecdote: Its long bill lets it reach prey buried in wet ground.

fields.summary: The Eurasian Oystercatcher is a black and white shore bird with a long orange bill. Its pink legs and loud calls catch your attention.
fields.behaviour: It eats shellfish, worms and other small animals. Depending on the prey, it uses its bill to probe, open or hammer.
fields.why_here: Mudflats, rocky coasts and beaches give it food. It can nest on the ground in open areas.
fields.migration: You can see it all year on some French coasts. Migrants and winter visitors join the birds that breed in the country.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are powerful, high and repeated. Groups can be very noisy, especially when they move.
fields.confusions: Its big orange bill, pink legs and black and white feathers easily set it apart from many other shorebirds.
fields.anecdote: Not all birds handle shellfish the same way: some hammer them, others pry open the shells.
fields.hint: My long orange bill and pink legs stand out on the shore.

fields.summary: The Western Bonelli's Warbler is a small bird of light woods. Its whitish belly contrasts with the greener tones of its back and rump.
fields.behaviour: It looks for small insects in the leaves. The male sings from branches, sometimes without showing himself.
fields.why_here: Bright woods, often on dry or sloping ground, give it food and shelter. Its nest is close to the ground.
fields.migration: It comes back to France in the warm season and leaves for Africa after breeding.
fields.by_ear: Its song is a short, dry trill, repeated at intervals. Its contact calls are more whistled.
fields.confusions: The Wood Warbler has more yellow on the face and throat. The Western Bonelli's Warbler looks paler underneath.
fields.anecdote: A bird almost invisible in the leaves can be found thanks to its little repeated trill.
fields.hint: My small dry trill rings out in sunny woods.

fields.summary: The Eurasian Stone-curlew is a bird of dry ground with earth-colored feathers. Its big yellow eyes give it a very special look.
fields.behaviour: It mostly looks for insects and other small prey on the ground. It is often more active at dusk and at night.
fields.why_here: Dry grassland, stony ground and some crops give it open spaces to hide and nest on the ground.
fields.migration: It stays in France mostly in the warm season. Some birds also stay in winter in good places.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are powerful and sad-sounding, often heard as night falls. They can carry far over quiet countryside.
fields.confusions: Plovers have a shape that is less tall on its legs. The very big yellow eyes and the sturdy bill help you recognize the Eurasian Stone-curlew.
fields.anecdote: Standing still on stony ground, it can be very hard to spot despite its size.
fields.hint: My big yellow eyes watch over dry ground at dusk.

fields.summary: The Greater White-fronted Goose is a grey goose whose adult has a white forehead. Uneven black marks cross its belly.
fields.behaviour: It grazes and eats seeds in open country. It gathers with other geese on feeding and resting areas.
fields.why_here: Meadows, fields and big lakes give it food and places to spend the night.
fields.migration: It visits France mostly in winter and during migration. How many you see varies with the region and the weather.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are loud, fairly high and often repeated in a group. Their rhythm can sound like laughter.
fields.confusions: The adult Greylag Goose has neither the white forehead nor the strong black marks on the belly. Young birds have less clear marks.
fields.anecdote: The dark patterns on the belly differ from one adult to another.
fields.hint: Dark, uneven marks cross my belly.

fields.summary: The Eurasian Treecreeper is a small speckled brown bird with a thin, curved bill. It explores the bark as it climbs up trunks.
fields.behaviour: It picks small animals out of cracks. Its stiff tail props it up against the tree.
fields.why_here: Forests rich in trees with rough bark give it food and shelter. It nests in cracks or behind loose bark.
fields.migration: It is usually present all year in its French breeding areas. You find it especially in forest areas and mountain regions.
fields.by_ear: Its song is a short, high, thin phrase. Calls and song are valuable for telling it from the Short-toed Treecreeper.
fields.confusions: The Short-toed Treecreeper looks very much like it. The voice and several details of the bill, claws and wings must be considered together.
fields.anecdote: It climbs up one trunk, then often flies down to the bottom of another to start again.
fields.hint: My tail props me up when I climb the bark.

fields.summary: The Red-throated Loon is a water bird with a thin, slightly upturned bill. In breeding plumage, a rusty patch marks its throat.
fields.behaviour: It dives to chase fish. Very at ease under water, it moves clumsily on dry land.
fields.why_here: In France, it mostly visits coastal waters in winter. It can also stop on big lakes.
fields.migration: It visits France mostly during migration and in the cold season. It breeds in regions further north.
fields.by_ear: It is often quiet on its winter waters. Sounds from the breeding grounds are not the best clues for a sighting in France.
fields.confusions: The Black-throated Loon has a stronger bill that is usually more level. The Red-throated Loon often seems to tip up the point of its bill.
fields.anecdote: Its legs, set far back, are made for swimming but make walking clumsy.
fields.hint: My thin bill tilts up over winter waters.

fields.summary: The Black-throated Loon is a diving bird with a straight bill. In breeding plumage, it combines a grey head, a black throat and a back with a contrasting pattern.
fields.behaviour: It chases fish under water. When it swims on the surface, its body stays fairly low in the water.
fields.why_here: In France, it mostly uses coastal waters and sometimes big lakes during its winter stay.
fields.migration: You find it in France mainly in winter and during migration. It breeds in regions further north.
fields.by_ear: It is often silent during its winter stay. Looking at the bill and the feathers helps more to identify it.
fields.confusions: The Red-throated Loon has a thinner bill, often held tilted up. In winter, the Black-throated Loon shows a sharper contrast between the dark neck and the pale throat.
fields.anecdote: Its feathers change a lot between the contrasting breeding look and the plainer winter one.
fields.hint: I chase fish under the water with a straight bill.

fields.summary: The Egyptian Goose is a big water bird with brown and beige feathers. A dark patch surrounds each eye.
fields.behaviour: It grazes and looks for seeds, often near water. Pairs can defend their territory fiercely.
fields.why_here: Ponds, parks and wetlands give it grass to eat and many kinds of places to nest.
fields.migration: Brought to Europe by people, it is present all year in some French areas. Birds can spread to new lakes and ponds.
fields.by_ear: The female makes powerful, rough calls. The male's voice is usually quieter and breathy.
fields.confusions: The Ruddy Shelduck is more evenly rusty. The Egyptian Goose has a dark patch around the eye and more mixed feathers.
fields.anecdote: It can nest high up, in a tree or on a building.
fields.hint: A brown mask surrounds each of my eyes.

fields.summary: A round field bird with an orange face and a grey chest. A brown horseshoe-shaped patch often marks its belly.
fields.behaviour: It walks with its family through crops and pecks at seeds, leaves and insects. The chicks mostly look for small insects.
fields.why_here: Farmed plains with grass strips, hedges and quiet edges give it food and shelter.
fields.migration: It stays all year in the French countryside, usually close to where it was born.
fields.by_ear: Its call is short, rasping and a little grating. You hear it especially at dusk.
fields.confusions: The Red-legged Partridge has a red bill and red legs, and a black pattern around the throat.
fields.anecdote: Outside the breeding season, family groups gather in small flocks.
fields.hint: I walk with my family through the fields, my face orange.

fields.summary: A small diving duck, russet brown. The adult male has a very pale eye, and a white patch shows under the tail.
fields.behaviour: It dives to take water plants and small animals. It likes to stay near the plants that line the water.
fields.why_here: It looks for ponds and marshes rich in plants, with patches of open water and reeds.
fields.migration: Birds can be seen in France in different seasons. Movements vary between populations.
fields.confusions: The male Tufted Duck is black and white. Here, the body stays russet brown and the head has no long crest.
fields.anecdote: The big white band on the wing becomes very visible when the bird takes off.
fields.hint: A wide white wing stripe shows when I take off.

fields.summary: The male is a duck with dazzling colors, with orange feathers standing up like little sails. The brown female has a thin white outline around the eye.
fields.behaviour: It looks for seeds, fruits and small animals at the water's edge. It perches easily in trees.
fields.why_here: Waters close to big trees suit it. It uses a tree hole for its nest.
fields.migration: Originally from Asia, it also lives wild in Europe after people brought it here. Birds settled in France can stay all year.
fields.confusions: The male Wood Duck also has a very colorful head, but not these big orange feathers standing up on the back.
fields.anecdote: The chicks leave the hole where they were born by jumping down to the ground.
fields.hint: The male wears two little orange sails on his back.

fields.summary: A stocky bird of open country, with a red bill and red legs. Its white throat is edged with black and its sides have wide stripes.
fields.behaviour: It mostly looks for food on the ground: seeds, shoots and small animals. It often prefers to run before it flies.
fields.why_here: Crops, vineyards and dry ground with bushes let it feed and hide its nest on the ground.
fields.migration: It stays in France all year. Its movements remain mostly local.
fields.by_ear: Its song is a run of rough, jerky notes that seem to speed up.
fields.confusions: The Grey Partridge has an orange face and does not have the same black collar around the throat.
fields.anecdote: Its brown feathers blend into dry earth as soon as it freezes.
fields.hint: I prefer to run before I fly, among the vines.

fields.summary: A small bird of cold regions, with lots of white in the wings. In winter, its feathers mix white, brown and rust.
fields.behaviour: It looks for seeds on the ground, often in a group. Flocks move together from one open spot to another.
fields.why_here: In France, beaches, dunes and open coastal ground give it seeds during the cold season.
fields.migration: It is mostly a winter visitor in France. It goes back to breed in northern regions in spring.
fields.confusions: The wide white patches on its wings set it apart from many small brown birds feeding on the ground.
fields.anecdote: The male has much more contrasting black and white feathers during the breeding season.
fields.hint: My white wings brighten the beaches in winter.

fields.summary: A tiny greenish bird with a long pale eyebrow and two pale bars on the wing. It keeps slipping through the leaves.
fields.behaviour: It checks leaves and twigs to pick off small insects. Its quick moves make it hard to follow.
fields.why_here: Trees and shrubs in gardens, woods and parks give it a resting stop when it shows up in France.
fields.migration: It nests in Asia. In France, it is mostly seen during the autumn passage, far from its usual migration route.
fields.by_ear: Its call is high, thin and rising, often easier to spot than the bird.
fields.confusions: Hume's Leaf Warbler looks very much like it. A detailed look and listening to the call help tell them apart.
fields.anecdote: A bird this small can make very long migration trips.
fields.hint: Two pale bars on my wing, I search the leaves.

fields.summary: A big streaky brown bird that lives hidden in the reeds. Its neck can stretch and its bill can point to the sky when it feels watched.
fields.behaviour: It moves slowly along the water's edge to catch fish, amphibians and other small animals.
fields.why_here: It needs fairly big flooded reedbeds, where it can hunt and hide.
fields.migration: Some birds stay in France all year. Others, from colder regions, spend the winter here.
fields.by_ear: The male makes a very low, hollow sound, like the noise you get blowing across a bottle.
fields.confusions: The Little Bittern is much smaller. The all streaky brown feathers help you recognize this resident of big reedbeds.
fields.anecdote: Standing still with its bill up, it lines up the stripes on its body with the reed stems.
fields.hint: Hidden in the reeds, I blow like a bottle.

fields.summary: A big duck with orange-rusty feathers and a paler head. Its wings show wide white patches in flight.
fields.behaviour: It grazes and pecks on banks or nearby land. It also takes small water animals.
fields.why_here: Open waters and grassy banks give it places to rest and feed.
fields.migration: In France, many birds come from introduced populations or from escapes from captivity. Some stay all year.
fields.confusions: The Common Shelduck has a mostly white body, a dark head and a red bill.
fields.anecdote: It can make its nest in a hole, sometimes far from water.
fields.hint: My orange body flies over the pond on white wings.

fields.summary: A big duck with a long red bill edged with small teeth. The male has a dark head and a very pale body; the female has a shaggy brown head.
fields.behaviour: It chases fish under water. Sometimes it looks below the surface before diving.
fields.why_here: Rivers and lakes full of fish suit it. To nest, it looks mainly for tree holes.
fields.migration: It is present all year in some French areas. In winter, birds from further north join the lakes and ponds.
fields.confusions: The female Red-breasted Merganser has a less sharp line between the brown head and the pale neck. The two species need careful watching.
fields.anecdote: The chicks can leave their nest in a tree by jumping to the ground.
fields.hint: My toothed bill holds slippery fish.

fields.summary: A diving duck of the north. The male has a dark head, a pale grey back and white sides; the female often has white around the bill.
fields.behaviour: It dives to look for shellfish and other small water animals. It likes to gather in flocks.
fields.why_here: In winter, bays, river mouths and big lakes give it food and rest.
fields.migration: It comes to France mostly in winter and goes back to its northern breeding areas in spring.
fields.confusions: The male Tufted Duck has a black back and a crest. This one has a finely patterned grey back and a head without a long crest.
fields.hint: My pale grey back sets me apart among the dark divers.

fields.summary: A big bird with a grey back and long legs. In adults, the often very white head and the long bill give a slender shape.
fields.behaviour: It takes fish, small animals and food scraps. It also visits farmland and inland waters.
fields.why_here: Big lakes, rivers, coasts and places rich in food can attract it.
fields.migration: Birds move to western Europe after breeding. In France, sightings are not limited to a single season.
fields.confusions: The European Herring Gull and the Yellow-legged Gull look very much like it. Age, shape and several feather details must be checked together.
fields.hint: My white head tops a long thin bill.

fields.summary: A small eagle with fairly wide wings. Some birds have a pale underside, others are almost all dark.
fields.behaviour: It hunts birds, small mammals and reptiles. It alternates gliding flight and quick attacks.
fields.why_here: It visits landscapes that mix woods for nesting and open spaces for hunting.
fields.migration: Most French nesting birds leave for Africa after summer and come back in spring. A few birds stay in winter.
fields.confusions: The Common Buzzard can have similar colors. You must watch the wings and tail in flight to avoid mixing them up.
fields.anecdote: The pale and dark birds really are the same species.
fields.hint: I glide, then attack fast.

fields.summary: A diving duck with a big head and a golden eye. The black and white male has a round white spot between the bill and the eye.
fields.behaviour: It dives to catch small water animals. During courtship, the male throws his head sharply back.
fields.why_here: Lakes and rivers are its feeding places. In its breeding areas, it uses tree holes.
fields.migration: You see it in France mostly in the cold season. Most visitors go back north in spring.
fields.confusions: The male Tufted Duck does not have the round white spot at the base of the bill and has a crest.
fields.anecdote: Its wingbeats can make a whistling sound you can hear in flight.
fields.hint: My wings whistle when I fly.

fields.summary: A big duck from tropical America. Farm birds often show white patches and bumpy red skin around the eyes.
fields.behaviour: It looks for plants, seeds and small animals in the water and on the banks. It can also perch.
fields.why_here: In France, you meet it mostly around farms and parks, sometimes free on lakes and ponds.
fields.migration: The birds seen in France are usually linked to farming. They do not follow a regular natural migration in the country.
fields.by_ear: It is fairly quiet: it hisses and makes low sounds rather than loud quacks.
fields.anecdote: The farm form comes from a wild bird that perches and nests in trees.
fields.hint: Bumpy red skin surrounds my eyes.

fields.summary: A goose with a white face, a black chest and a barred grey back. It often feeds in tight groups.
fields.behaviour: It grazes short grass and looks for plants on coastal meadows or crops.
fields.why_here: Open meadows near water let it eat while watching its surroundings.
fields.migration: Northern populations migrate and can reach France in winter. Birds from introduced populations are also present all year.
fields.confusions: The Canada Goose has only a white band under the head, and its neck is longer.
fields.anecdote: In some Arctic regions, the chicks leave the nest by jumping off a cliff.
fields.hint: My white face stands out against my black chest.

fields.summary: A small sea gull with a grey back and black legs. Adults have black wingtips, as if dipped in ink.
fields.behaviour: It mostly catches small fish near the surface and spends a lot of time at sea.
fields.why_here: Coastal cliffs give it narrow ledges to nest in colonies, above the water.
fields.migration: It nests on some French coasts, then spreads widely at sea. Its travels make it harder to see from land outside the breeding season.
fields.by_ear: In the colony, its repeated calls are loud and nasal.
fields.confusions: The adult Black-headed Gull has red on the bill and legs. Here, the bill is yellow and the legs are dark.
fields.anecdote: Its nest can fit on a tiny cliff ledge.
fields.hint: I nest on a ledge above the waves.

fields.summary: A small brown bird of tall grass, mostly remarkable for its very varied song. It often stays hidden in the plants.
fields.behaviour: It catches insects among stems and leaves. The male sings for a long time from a hidden perch.
fields.why_here: Ditches, stream edges and wet wasteland rich in tall plants suit it.
fields.migration: It spends the warm season in Europe and winters in Africa. It arrives in France in spring and leaves after breeding.
fields.by_ear: Its lively song strings together whistles, rasping notes and copies of other birds.
fields.confusions: The Eurasian Reed Warbler looks very much like it. The song and the habitat are often more useful than the color of the feathers.
fields.anecdote: It can add to its song the sounds of birds heard during its stay in Africa.
fields.hint: In tall grass, I gather voices from far away.

fields.summary: A small bird with a grey head and a black mask. Its warm brown back goes with a light, lively shape.
fields.behaviour: It looks for insects and seeds in reeds, trees and bushes near water.
fields.why_here: Wetlands with willows and reeds give it food and materials to build its nest.
fields.migration: Movements vary between populations. In France, you can see it in different seasons, especially in wetlands during migration.
fields.by_ear: Its call is a thin, drawn-out, slightly sad little whistle.
fields.confusions: The Bearded Reedling has a long tail and, in the male, black mustaches rather than a band over the eyes.
fields.anecdote: Its hanging nest looks like a soft purse, with a little tube for an entrance.
fields.hint: I wear a black mask on a grey head.

fields.summary: A small water bird with grey wings. In summer, its black cap, white cheeks and dark belly make a contrasting face.
fields.behaviour: It flies over the water to pick insects and small prey, sometimes brushing the surface.
fields.why_here: Shallow ponds with lots of floating plants let it feed and build its nest.
fields.migration: It comes back to France in the warm season and leaves for warmer regions after breeding.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are short and rasping, often repeated as it flies over the marsh.
fields.confusions: In summer, the Black Tern has a dark head and neck. Here, the cheeks stay white.
fields.anecdote: Its nest rests on the floating plants of ponds.
fields.hint: In summer, my white cheeks frame a dark throat.

fields.summary: A small falcon with long wings. The adult male is dark grey with red legs; the female has an orange underside and a grey back.
fields.behaviour: It catches big insects in flight or on the ground. Sometimes it hunts in a group over open country.
fields.why_here: Meadows, crops and wetlands rich in insects can host it during its travels.
fields.migration: It spends the winter in Africa. France lies mostly on its passage routes, with sightings in spring and after summer.
fields.confusions: The Eurasian Hobby has a white throat and clear dark mustaches. The adult male here has much more evenly grey feathers.
fields.anecdote: It uses nests already built by other birds, especially in crow colonies.
fields.hint: I hunt big insects, sometimes in a group.

fields.summary: A big brown bird of prey with wide wings, with golden glints on the back of the neck. It soars above slopes and valleys.
fields.behaviour: It mostly hunts mammals and birds, but also eats animals that are already dead.
fields.why_here: Mountains with cliffs and open spaces give it nest sites and wide hunting grounds.
fields.migration: Pairs settled in France usually stay in their territory all year. Young birds travel more.
fields.confusions: The Griffon Vulture has a smaller head, a long neck and a much shorter tail in flight.
fields.anecdote: A pair can keep several big nests and choose one to breed in.
fields.hint: I glide above hillsides and valleys.

fields.summary: A small streaky bird, topped with a red patch, with a dark chin. Males can also have a pinkish chest.
fields.behaviour: It picks small seeds, sometimes hanging from twigs. It likes to feed in flocks.
fields.why_here: Birches, alders and other trees with small seeds attract this bird of cool regions.
fields.migration: Movements depend on the populations and on the food available. Northern birds can come to France in the cold season.
fields.confusions: The Common Linnet does not have the small black chin. For dull-colored birds, you must look carefully at the head.
fields.anecdote: Its short bill lets it pull tiny seeds out of the dry fruits of trees.
fields.hint: I hang from twigs to pick tiny seeds.

fields.summary: A big, dark sea duck with a white band on each wing that shows in flight. The male also has a small white mark near his eye.
fields.behaviour: She dives to find shellfish and other animals living underwater. She often rests far out at sea in a group.
fields.why_here: Coastal waters with a seabed full of shellfish give her food for the winter.
fields.migration: She shows up in France mostly in winter, far from her northern breeding grounds.
fields.confusions: The Common Scoter does not have the big white band on the wing.
fields.anecdote: The white band on her wings can stay partly hidden while she floats.
fields.hint: My dark wings reveal a big white window.

fields.summary: A small diving bird with a sharply two-toned head in winter. In breeding plumage, it has golden tufts behind the eyes and a reddish neck.
fields.behaviour: It catches small water animals by diving, and it swims very low on the water.
fields.why_here: In winter, sheltered bays and some large French lakes give it places to fish.
fields.migration: It is mostly a cold-season visitor in France and breeds mainly farther north.
fields.confusions: The Black-necked Grebe has a thinner, slightly upturned bill. In winter, the shape of the head and bill helps tell them apart.
fields.anecdote: Its toes have flaps along the edges that help push it through the water.
fields.hint: In summer, two golden tufts frame my red eyes.

fields.summary: A tiny tern with narrow wings. In summer it has a white forehead under a black cap, and a yellow bill with a dark tip.
fields.behaviour: It flies over the water, sometimes hovers in place, then dives to catch small fish.
fields.why_here: Open sandbanks and gravel banks are where it nests, on the coast or along big rivers.
fields.migration: It comes back to France in spring and leaves after breeding to spend the winter on warmer coasts.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are high and short, often made in flight.
fields.confusions: The Common Tern is bigger and has no white forehead in summer plumage.
fields.anecdote: Its eggs blend in with the grains of sand and little pebbles.
fields.hint: A white forehead tops my yellow, dark-tipped bill.

fields.summary: A very big seabird with an almost black back, a white head and a yellow bill. Its legs are pink.
fields.behaviour: It takes fish, shellfish, scraps and sometimes other birds. It can steal food from its neighbors.
fields.why_here: It lives on coasts, in harbors and on small islands, and sometimes visits inland waters.
fields.migration: It is here all year on French coasts. Some birds move around after breeding and head to other areas in winter.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are deep and powerful, lower than those of many nearby coastal birds.
fields.confusions: The Lesser Black-backed Gull is less bulky and has yellow legs as an adult.
fields.anecdote: Its large size often lets it take charge around a source of food.
fields.hint: Pink legs and a yellow bill: I rule the harbor.

fields.summary: A big night bird of prey with orange eyes and upright tufts of feathers on its head. Its brown feathers blend in with rocks.
fields.behaviour: It hunts at night for mammals and birds. It finds its prey by hearing and sight.
fields.why_here: Cliffs, quarries and rocky slopes give it shelter close to open hunting grounds.
fields.migration: It usually stays in France all year. Young birds leave the territory where they were born.
fields.by_ear: The male gives a very low, deep hoot, repeated with pauses.
fields.confusions: The Long-eared Owl is much smaller and slimmer. Compare the overall shape and the power of the song too.
fields.anecdote: The tufts on its head are feathers. They are not its ears.
fields.hint: My orange eyes shine between two tufts of feathers.

fields.summary: A small brown bird that hides at the foot of the reeds. Its non-stop song sounds more like an insect than a bird.
fields.behaviour: It looks for small animals in thick plants, near the water or the ground.
fields.why_here: Big wet reedbeds with low, tangled plants give it food and hiding places.
fields.migration: It comes back to France in spring and leaves for Africa after breeding.
fields.by_ear: Its song is a long, steady purr, deep for such a small bird, that seems to run on without stopping.
fields.confusions: The Grasshopper Warbler has small spots on its back. Its mechanical song is higher.
fields.anecdote: A still, well-hidden bird can fill a whole reedbed with its song.
fields.hint: I make the reeds purr like a hidden insect.

fields.summary: A sea duck whose male is almost completely black. The female is brown, with paler cheeks.
fields.behaviour: She dives to take shellfish and other small animals from the bottom. The birds often gather in big flocks at sea.
fields.why_here: Coastal waters rich in shellfish give her good feeding areas.
fields.migration: Some birds pass through and spend the winter on French coasts. Some also stay at sea outside the winter.
fields.confusions: The Velvet Scoter has a big white band on the wing, which is missing here.
fields.anecdote: Big gatherings can form at sea while the birds grow new flight feathers.
fields.hint: The all-black male dives among the waves.

fields.summary: A big diving bird with a strong bill. In summer its black-and-white feathers show a checkered pattern on the back. In winter it turns gray and white.
fields.behaviour: It chases fish underwater, pushing itself with its feet. It can swim far away below the surface before popping up again.
fields.why_here: Sheltered bays and coastal waters are its fishing spots during its stays in France.
fields.migration: It visits French coasts mostly in the cold season. It nests much farther north, on lakes.
fields.confusions: The Arctic Loon is slimmer and has a less powerful bill. The shape of the head and bill helps tell them apart.
fields.anecdote: Its feet are set far back. They are great for swimming but make walking hard.
fields.hint: My summer back looks like a black-and-white checkerboard.

fields.summary: A big brown goose with a long black neck. A wide white band runs under the chin and up the cheeks.
fields.behaviour: It grazes on lawns, meadows and crops. Families travel together between the water and grassy ground.
fields.why_here: Lakes, parks and rivers surrounded by grass give it food and places to rest.
fields.migration: Brought to Europe by people, it lives in France all year. Birds may move to another body of water depending on food and the seasons.
fields.by_ear: It gives loud, nasal honks, often in flight or within the group.
fields.confusions: The Barnacle Goose is smaller, with a mostly white face and a black chest.
fields.anecdote: Both parents go with the young and defend them while they travel.
fields.hint: A white chinstrap crosses my long black neck.

fields.summary: A small, tawny bird with a very long tail. The male has a gray head and two big black marks hanging down like a mustache.
fields.behaviour: She climbs between the stems and looks for small animals. In winter, reed seeds make up a big part of her diet.
fields.why_here: Large reedbeds give it food, shelter and supports for its nest.
fields.migration: It can stay all year in French reedbeds. Some groups move to other marshes.
fields.by_ear: Its small, clear, metallic calls often let you spot a flock before you see it.
fields.confusions: The Penduline Tit has a black mask over its eyes and a much shorter tail.
fields.anecdote: Its diet changes with the seasons, shifting from insects to seeds when the cold arrives.
fields.hint: My very long tail sways among the stems.

fields.summary: A small brown water bird dotted with pale spots. It slips quietly through flooded grass and rarely shows itself in the open.
fields.behaviour: She pecks at small animals and seeds in the mud and very shallow water.
fields.why_here: Wet meadows and marshes with low plants suit it, with water close to the ground.
fields.migration: A migrant, it appears mostly while passing through and in the warm season. Its presence can change a lot from one marsh to another.
fields.by_ear: The male repeats a short, clear whistle, often heard at night.
fields.confusions: The Water Rail has a much longer red bill. Here, the bill is short and the feathers are dotted with pale spots.
fields.anecdote: Its night song helps find birds that you almost never see.
fields.hint: My little night whistles come from flooded grass.

fields.summary: A northern sea duck with bold, contrasting feathers. The male has long, thin feathers in the middle of his tail.
fields.behaviour: She dives to find small water animals and can feed far from shore.
fields.why_here: Coastal waters and large lakes serve as a rest stop or a winter home.
fields.migration: She is mainly a winter visitor in France. She breeds in the Arctic.
fields.confusions: The male's long tail is a good clue. Females and young birds need a closer look.
fields.anecdote: Its feathers change a lot through the year, which changes how it looks.

fields.summary: A big sea duck with an angular profile. The male is black and white with a green tint on the nape. The female is brown with fine bars.
fields.behaviour: He dives to take mussels and other animals from the bottom, and can swallow them whole with their shells.
fields.why_here: Rocky coasts and waters rich in shellfish suit it. It nests on the ground near the shore.
fields.migration: It can be seen all year on some French coasts. Movements and numbers change with the seasons.
fields.by_ear: The male makes soft, deep calls during his courtship display.
fields.anecdote: The female lines her nest with soft down taken from her own body.

fields.summary: A tiny heron of the reeds. The male is black and buff, while the female is browner and streaked.
fields.behaviour: It catches small fish, insects and amphibians, creeping carefully along the water's edge.
fields.why_here: It looks for marshes and ponds with thick plants, where reeds and bushes give it perches and hiding places.
fields.migration: It spends the warm season in France and winters in Africa, coming back in spring.
fields.by_ear: The male makes a dull, repeated note that is fairly quiet and easy to miss.
fields.confusions: The Eurasian Bittern is much bigger and has streaked brown feathers all over.
fields.anecdote: Its long toes let it grip several reed stems at once.
fields.hint: My long toes grip the stems above the water.

fields.summary: A pale seabird with a shaggy black cap. Its black bill has a small yellow tip.
fields.behaviour: She spots fish from the air, then dives into the water. She often fishes near the coast.
fields.why_here: Coastal waters give it fish, and bare little islands hold its colonies.
fields.migration: It nests on some French coasts. Some birds pass through during migration, and some stay on the shore for the winter.
fields.by_ear: Its harsh, rolling cries carry far over the beaches.
fields.confusions: The Common Tern has a red bill in summer. Here, the long dark bill with a yellow tip is a good clue.
fields.anecdote: Adults can offer a fish to their partner during courtship.
fields.hint: The yellow tip on my black bill points to my catch.

fields.summary: A big shorebird with a long, slightly upturned bill. Its feathers turn reddish-brown for breeding, then grayer in winter.
fields.behaviour: She pushes her bill into mud or sand to find worms and small animals.
fields.why_here: Estuaries, bays and mudflats uncovered at low tide give her food.
fields.migration: She nests in northern lands and visits France while passing through and in winter. Some birds can also stay on the coast in summer.
fields.confusions: The Black-tailed Godwit has a wide white bar on the wing and a very contrasting tail. Here, the tail is finely barred.
fields.anecdote: Some populations make very long trips over the ocean without landing.
fields.hint: My long, slightly upturned bill probes the mud.

fields.summary: A green bird with a long pointed tail and a red bill. The adult male has a thin dark and pinkish collar.
fields.behaviour: She eats seeds, fruit and buds. She moves around in noisy groups and gathers to sleep together.
fields.why_here: Parks and gardens with big trees give it food and holes to nest in.
fields.migration: Descended from birds brought in by people, it lives all year in several French cities and regions.
fields.by_ear: Its sharp, piercing screams, repeated in flight, give it away from far off.
fields.anecdote: In the evening, groups can meet up in big shared roosts.
fields.hint: Green and noisy, I cross the parks with my long tail.

fields.summary: A big white bird with a straight neck and a yellow and black bill. The yellow area stretches forward in a point along the bill.
fields.behaviour: It mostly eats plants, in the water or on farmland. Groups often stay together as they travel.
fields.why_here: Calm bodies of water and nearby fields give it rest and food.
fields.migration: It visits France mostly in winter, after leaving breeding areas farther north.
fields.by_ear: Its powerful, clear calls sound like trumpet blasts.
fields.confusions: The Bewick's Swan is smaller and usually has less yellow on the bill. The Mute Swan has an orange bill.
fields.anecdote: Its calls help the members of a group stay in touch during flight.
fields.hint: My yellow and black bill goes with trumpet calls.

fields.summary: A big water bird, almost all black, with a long neck and a red bill. Its big white flight feathers show when it opens its wings.
fields.behaviour: It mostly eats water plants, dipping its neck into the water. It also grazes on the banks.
fields.why_here: Ponds, lakes and park pools give it calm water and plants.
fields.migration: Originally from Australia, it was brought to Europe by people. Birds seen in France come from these introductions and can stay all year.
fields.confusions: The adult Mute Swan is white and has a black bump at the base of the bill.
fields.anecdote: Its wings hide big white feathers, almost invisible while it swims.
fields.hint: When I spread my wings, big white feathers appear.

fields.summary: A gray-brown goose with a small dark bill banded with pink. Its legs are pink and its head is darker than its back.
fields.behaviour: She grazes on grasses and eats plants in meadows and fields, often in a group.
fields.why_here: Farmland close to quiet resting places can welcome it during the bad season.
fields.migration: It is an uncommon winter visitor in France, coming from populations that breed in the north.
fields.confusions: The Bean Goose usually has orange legs and a longer bill. Look closely at these colors.
fields.anecdote: Families can stay together during their winter travels.

fields.summary: A diving bird with a fairly thick neck and a strong bill, yellow at the base. In summer, its reddish neck contrasts with its gray cheeks.
fields.behaviour: It dives to catch fish and small water animals. It keeps vanishing under the surface while looking for food.
fields.why_here: Sheltered coastal waters and large lakes are its refuge outside the breeding season.
fields.migration: It is seen in France mostly in the cold season and while passing through.
fields.confusions: The Great Crested Grebe has a longer, thinner neck. In winter, the yellow base of the bill is a useful clue.
fields.anecdote: In summer feathers, the reddish neck changes its rather dull winter look.
fields.hint: My strong bill, yellow at the base, keeps vanishing under the surface.

fields.summary: A small bird of rocky slopes with a gray head lined with black stripes. Its belly and back have reddish-brown tones.
fields.behaviour: It looks for seeds and small insects on the ground, between stones and grasses.
fields.why_here: Sunny hillsides with boulders, bushes and thin plant cover give it food and shelter.
fields.migration: It lives all year in its French regions. Some birds move down to lower areas in winter.
fields.by_ear: Its song is a short phrase of thin, tinkling notes.
fields.confusions: The Cirl Bunting has yellow on the head and underneath. Here, the gray head striped with black is the clue.
fields.anecdote: It can find food on slopes where plants look very sparse.
