fields.hint: Black stripes line my gray head.

fields.summary: A small yellowish-green bird with a fairly wide bill. Its song, full of imitations, grabs more attention than its feathers.
fields.behaviour: She catches insects in trees and bushes. She often sings hidden among the leaves.
fields.why_here: Light woods, forest edges and leafy groves give it insects and places to nest.
fields.migration: She comes back from Africa in spring and leaves after the warm season. In France, she is found mostly in some eastern and northern regions.
fields.by_ear: Its song mixes scratchy notes, whistles and many imitations, with repeated patterns.
fields.confusions: The Melodious Warbler looks very much like it. The wing length and the song help tell them apart.
fields.anecdote: She can borrow part of her song from other species.
fields.hint: I mix other birds' voices into my own whistles.

fields.summary: A brown bird with broad wings, often seen near cliffs. Small white spots show in its tail when it spreads it.
fields.behaviour: She catches insects in flight, often flying along rock walls and buildings.
fields.why_here: Cliffs, bridges and sheltered walls give it places to attach its mud nest.
fields.migration: It can stay in France all year, mostly in mild regions. Birds leave cold areas or move to lower ground in winter.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are short, rather dry and quiet.
fields.confusions: The Sand Martin has a dark band across the chest and lacks the small white spots in the tail.
fields.anecdote: It also uses human buildings that remind it of a rock wall.
fields.hint: Small white windows pierce my brown tail.

fields.summary: A plump bird with pinkish-brown feathers and a crest. It wears a black mask, a yellow tail tip and small red decorations.
fields.behaviour: It swallows berries and fruit, often in flocks. It also takes insects in the warm season.
fields.why_here: Trees and bushes loaded with fruit can draw it into gardens and streets.
fields.migration: It nests in northern forests. Some years, groups come to France in winter when their travels push them south.
fields.by_ear: Its fine, shivering little trills sound like tiny bells.
fields.anecdote: The small red tips on its wings look like drops of wax.
fields.hint: Crest up, I make the berry-laden trees ring.

fields.summary: A small diving duck. The white male has black lines on his body and around his eyes. The female has a brown cap and white cheeks.
fields.behaviour: It catches small animals underwater, especially fish in winter.
fields.why_here: Lakes, ponds and calm rivers are its fishing places.
fields.migration: It comes to France mostly in the cold season and goes back to northern forests to breed.
fields.confusions: The female Goosander is bigger and has a much longer bill. Here, the shape is more compact.
fields.anecdote: In its breeding areas, it can nest in a tree hole.
fields.hint: The male looks drawn in black ink on white.

fields.summary: A small wading bird, golden buff when it perches. In flight, it surprises you with almost completely white wings.
fields.behaviour: It waits or walks slowly in shallow water to catch insects, small fish and amphibians.
fields.why_here: Marshes, rice fields and shallow ponds give it good hunting grounds.
fields.migration: It comes back from Africa in the warm season and leaves after breeding. In France, it is found mostly in southern wetlands.
fields.confusions: The Western Cattle Egret is mostly white when perched. This one looks much more golden-brown before it spreads its wings.
fields.anecdote: Its look changes suddenly at takeoff, when its white wings become visible.
fields.hint: Beige at rest, I reveal white wings as I take off.

fields.summary: A tiny shorebird with a gray-brown back and rather pale legs. It moves quietly along the water.
fields.behaviour: It pecks at small animals on wet mud and in very shallow water.
fields.why_here: Muddy edges of ponds, marshes and basins give it stops to refuel.
fields.migration: It nests in northern lands and crosses France mostly during spring and late-summer migration.
fields.confusions: The Little Stint usually has dark legs and a livelier manner. Small brown birds still need careful watching.
fields.anecdote: The white feathers on the sides of its tail can be seen when it takes off.
fields.hint: I slip along the mud on my small pale legs.

fields.summary: A small bird of Mediterranean scrub. The male has a black head and a white throat, with a red ring around the eye.
fields.behaviour: She catches insects among the leaves and also eats small fruit. She often slips into the heart of the bushes.
fields.why_here: Scrubland, dry shrubland, hedges and thick gardens give it food and hiding places.
fields.migration: It lives all year in its French regions, mostly near the Mediterranean.
fields.by_ear: Its quick, dry calls sound like a little crackle. The song mixes scratchy notes with more musical parts.
fields.confusions: The Eurasian Blackcap has only a dark cap and no red ring around the eye.
fields.anecdote: Even in a small garden, dense bushes can give it shelter.
fields.hint: My red-ringed eye watches over the scrub.

fields.summary: A stocky bird with bright colors: blue head and belly, reddish-brown back. In flight, its wings show several shades of blue.
fields.behaviour: It watches for big insects from a branch or a wire, then drops to the ground to grab them.
fields.why_here: Open countryside with old hollow trees, meadows and crops gives it food and holes to nest in.
fields.migration: It comes back from Africa in spring and leaves after summer. In France, it is found mostly in southern regions.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are rough and scratchy, far from the softness of its colors.
fields.anecdote: During courtship, it does acrobatics and tumbles in mid-air.
fields.hint: My blue wings perform acrobatics above the fields.

fields.summary: A very big bird of prey with broad wings and a massive bill. The adult has a short, wedge-shaped white tail.
fields.behaviour: It catches fish and water birds, and also eats dead animals. It can take advantage of other birds' catches.
fields.why_here: Big lakes, rivers and wetlands give it food, with tall trees to perch or nest in.
fields.migration: Birds are here in different seasons in France. Some visitors arrive in winter, while others can settle for good.
fields.confusions: The Golden Eagle has a proportionally longer tail and lacks the huge yellow bill of the adult.
fields.anecdote: Young birds do not have the fully white tail of the adults right away.

fields.summary: A small gray-brown bird with a black cap and bib. Its pale cheeks contrast with the dark top of the head.
fields.behaviour: She looks for insects, spiders and seeds on branches. She can hide food to eat later.
fields.why_here: Cool woods with dead trees and soft wood let it find food and dig its nest.
fields.migration: It mostly stays put in its French regions. Movements are usually local.
fields.by_ear: Its calls include nasal, drawn-out notes. The song is made of little repeated whistles.
fields.confusions: The Marsh Tit looks very much like it. The voice is often more helpful than the small differences in feathers.
fields.anecdote: She can dig her own hole in very soft, rotting wood.
fields.hint: I dig my shelter in softened wood.

fields.summary: A small, dark goose with a short neck, marked with a small white patch on the adult. It likes the seaside.
fields.behaviour: It grazes on sea plants and grasses. Groups follow the food that the tide offers.
fields.why_here: Shallow bays, seagrass beds and coastal meadows give it food in winter.
fields.migration: It comes to France mostly in the cold season, then goes back to the Arctic to breed.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are low, rolling and fairly soft, often traded within the group.
fields.confusions: The Barnacle Goose has a mostly white face. Here, the head stays black and only a small pale mark decorates the neck.
fields.anecdote: Underwater meadows of plants called eelgrass are an important food for many wintering groups.
fields.hint: My little white collar goes with my meals in the seagrass.

fields.summary: A black seabird with green shine and a thin, hooked bill. During breeding, a small crest stands up on its forehead.
fields.behaviour: It dives from the surface to chase fish. It fishes mostly at sea, often near rocky coasts.
fields.why_here: Cliffs and rocky islets are its resting spots and nesting sites.
fields.migration: It is here all year on some French coasts. Young birds may scatter far from where they were born.
fields.confusions: The Great Cormorant is bulkier and has a thicker bill. Here, the shape and neck are slimmer.
fields.anecdote: It builds its nest on rocks, on a ledge, in a crack or in a cliff shelter.
fields.hint: A small crest stands on my fisher's forehead.

fields.summary: A small bird of low thickets with a long tail that is often cocked up. Its wine-brown underparts contrast with a dark gray back.
fields.behaviour: She looks for small insects in bushes and moves under cover, close to the ground.
fields.why_here: Heaths with gorse and thick scrubland give it shelter, food and places to nest.
fields.migration: It mostly stays in France all year. Harsh winters can be hard on this thicket bird.
fields.by_ear: Its short song is scratchy and hurried, mixed with clearer little notes.
fields.confusions: The Sardinian Warbler has a clearer white throat and a tail that is shorter compared with its body.
fields.anecdote: She can go from bush to bush almost without leaving their protective cover.
fields.hint: My long tail sticks out above the prickly gorse.

fields.summary: A big white seabird with black wingtips. The adult has a yellow-tinted head and a long, pointed bill.
fields.behaviour: It spots fish from the air, folds its wings and plunges into the sea. It can chase its prey underwater.
fields.why_here: Waters full of fish give it food. Islets and cliffs hold very crowded colonies.
fields.migration: You can see it all year off the French coasts. Birds spread out more at sea after breeding.
fields.confusions: Young birds are brown and slowly get paler. The shape with long, pointed wings is still a good clue.
fields.anecdote: Young birds take several years to get the white feathers of the adults.
fields.hint: I fold my wings to plunge like an arrow.

fields.summary: A bird of open spaces with a wide white eyebrow. In breeding plumage, a thin pale line separates the gray chest from the reddish-brown belly.
fields.behaviour: It runs, stops, and picks up small animals from the ground, especially insects.
fields.why_here: Short grass, open plateaus and farmland are its rest stops on its journeys.
fields.migration: In France, it is seen mostly during migration, especially in late summer. It breeds mainly in northern and mountain regions.
fields.confusions: The European Golden Plover lacks the same wide white eyebrow and the same chest pattern in breeding plumage.
fields.anecdote: The male usually sits on the eggs and looks after the chicks.
fields.hint: My wide white eyebrow lights up the treeless plateaus.

fields.summary: A small gray cliff bird with a long, thin bill. Its rounded wings show bright red when it opens them.
fields.behaviour: It explores cracks in the rock to find insects and spiders, moving along in little hops.
fields.why_here: Rock faces and gorges give it food and holes. In winter, it can also visit walls, quarries and monuments.
fields.migration: It lives in the mountains during breeding. In winter, some birds come down to cliffs and buildings at lower heights.
fields.anecdote: Opening its red wings again and again makes it look like a butterfly on the rock.
fields.hint: My red wings flash against the gray rock.

fields.summary: A very big bird of prey with a brown body, a pale head and a pale ruff of feathers. Its long wings let it glide for a long time.
fields.behaviour: It eats dead animals. It finds carcasses by crossing huge areas and watching other birds.
fields.why_here: Cliffs give it places to rest and nest, close to open land where herds roam.
fields.migration: Adults living in France usually stay in their region, but make long trips to feed. Young birds travel more.
fields.confusions: The Golden Eagle has a more prominent head and a longer tail. Here, the small head and short tail help in flight.
fields.anecdote: It rises on columns of warm air, which lets it gain height without flapping its wings all the time.
fields.hint: I clean up the mountain by eating dead animals.

fields.summary: A big tern with a heavy red bill, gray wings and a black cap. Its shape is powerful for a bird of this group.
fields.behaviour: She catches fish by diving from the air and can fish in fresh water as well as at sea.
fields.why_here: Lagoons, big ponds, lakes and estuaries give it fishing places during its travels.
fields.migration: In France, it is seen mostly while passing through in the warm season, between its breeding and winter homes.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are loud and harsh, with a deep voice.
fields.confusions: The Sandwich Tern has a much thinner black bill tipped with yellow. Here, the big red bill is a clear clue.
fields.anecdote: Its massive bill stays visible from far away, even when the bird rests among other species.
fields.hint: My big red bill rules the group on the beach.

fields.summary: A bird with long, pointed wings and a forked tail. The lower back and the nape are tinted reddish-brown.
fields.behaviour: She catches insects in flight and can hunt over open spaces or near cliffs.
fields.why_here: Warm regions with rocky shelters, bridges and buildings give it places to build its mud nest.
fields.migration: A migrant, it shows up in France in the warm season, mostly in the south, then heads south again.
fields.confusions: The Barn Swallow has a dark red throat. Here, the reddish-brown lower back is a precious clue when it banks in flight.
fields.anecdote: Its closed nest has an entrance stretched into a little mud tunnel.
fields.hint: My mud nest has a little entrance tunnel.

fields.summary: A bird of prey from cold regions with broad wings and often pale feathers. Its legs are covered with feathers down to the toes.
fields.behaviour: She hunts small mammals in open spaces. She can hover in place, flapping her wings, to watch the ground.
fields.why_here: Open plains, fields and meadows can welcome it in winter.
fields.migration: It nests in the north and visits France only in small numbers, mainly in the cold season.
fields.confusions: The Common Buzzard comes in many colors. The feathered legs and the tail pattern help spot this northern visitor.
fields.anecdote: The feathers covering its legs are a remarkable trait of this cold-region bird.
fields.hint: Feathers cover me down to my toes.

fields.summary: A duck with bright colors on the male, a long crest and white lines on the head. The brown female has a white outline around the eye.
fields.behaviour: He eats seeds, fruit and small animals in the water or on the banks. He likes to perch in trees.
fields.why_here: Wooded ponds and tree-lined rivers suit it. It nests in a hole.
fields.migration: Native to North America, it is seen in France mostly because of introductions or escapes from captivity.
fields.confusions: The male Mandarin Duck has big orange feathers standing up on the back. Females are harder to tell apart.
fields.anecdote: The ducklings jump out of the tree hole where they were born to join their mother.
fields.hint: White lines mark the male's crested head.

fields.summary: A brown goose with a dark bill marked with orange and orange legs. It often feeds in flocks in open spaces.
fields.behaviour: She eats plants in meadows and crops, then heads to a quiet place to rest.
fields.why_here: Fields near lakes and wetlands can give it a winter stop.
fields.migration: It breeds in northern regions and can reach France in winter.
fields.confusions: The Taiga Bean Goose looks extremely similar. The shape of the head and bill must be studied carefully, and a faraway view is often not enough.
fields.hint: My dark bill has an orange touch, like my feet.

fields.summary: A black-and-white bird of old trees with a red cap. Its pale belly is finely streaked and turns pink toward the tail.
fields.behaviour: It picks insects from bark and branches, searching the crevices. It taps wood less hard than other nearby species.
fields.why_here: Old leafy forests, especially rich in oaks, give it food and good nesting trees.
fields.migration: It stays in France all year and usually remains in its forest area.
fields.by_ear: Its spring call is whiny and nasal. It drums little, compared with some other trunk dwellers.
fields.confusions: The adult Great Spotted Woodpecker does not have a fully red cap. A young one can have one, so look more closely.
fields.anecdote: Both the male and the female wear a red cap.
fields.hint: My red cap explores the crevices of old oaks.

fields.summary: A small shorebird that swims very well. In summer, its underparts turn reddish-brown. In winter, it looks mostly gray and white.
fields.behaviour: It takes tiny animals from the water's surface. It can spin around while swimming to bring its food up.
fields.why_here: Outside breeding, it lives mostly at sea. Storms can bring it closer to French coasts.
fields.migration: It breeds in the Arctic and passes offshore during migration. In France, it is noticed especially after spells of bad weather.
fields.confusions: The Red-necked Phalarope has a thinner, needle-like bill. Here, the bill is shorter and thicker.
fields.anecdote: The male sits on the eggs and looks after the chicks.
fields.hint: I spin on the water to bring up my meal.

fields.summary: A black bird with glossy shine, a long curved red bill and red legs. It flits about easily near cliffs.
fields.behaviour: It digs in the ground and short grass to catch insects and other small animals.
fields.why_here: Cliffs near short grass or pastures give it holes to nest in and places to feed.
fields.migration: It lives all year in its French regions. Its movements mostly follow local food.
fields.by_ear: Its cries are clear, loud and piercing, often called out during its acrobatics.
fields.confusions: The Alpine Chough has a shorter yellow bill. Both have black feathers and red legs.
fields.anecdote: It can do spectacular dives and flips in the air currents.

fields.summary: A stocky shorebird with a straight bill. Its feathers are pale gray in winter and turn reddish-brown underneath for breeding.
fields.behaviour: It mostly looks for small shellfish on mudflats and beaches, often in tight groups.
fields.why_here: Big bays and estuaries give it huge feeding areas at low tide.
fields.migration: It nests in the Arctic and visits France while passing through and in winter. Some birds can also stay on the coast in summer.
fields.confusions: The Dunlin has a longer, often curved bill. This one looks heavier, with a fairly short bill.
fields.anecdote: It can swallow small shellfish whole, and the shell is then crushed inside its body.
fields.hint: Pale gray in winter, I wear a rusty belly in summer.

fields.summary: A big white water bird with a neck fairly short for a swan. The bill is mostly black, with an amount of yellow that varies between populations.
fields.behaviour: It eats water plants and also grazes in fields and meadows.
fields.why_here: Calm waters and nearby farmland give it places to rest and feed.
fields.migration: Visitors in France arrive mostly in winter and go back to the Arctic in spring.
fields.confusions: The Whooper Swan is bigger and usually has a larger yellow area on the bill.
fields.anecdote: The yellow and black patterns on the bill differ from one bird to another.
fields.hint: My mostly black bill sets off my white shape in winter.

fields.summary: A small bird of prey, pale gray and white, with black marks on the shoulders. Its red eyes can be seen from close up.
fields.behaviour: It hunts small rodents, from a perch or by hovering in the air before dropping on its prey.
fields.why_here: Open countryside with meadows, crops and lone trees gives it hunting grounds and nesting spots.
fields.migration: It lives all year in its French regions. Its movements can follow how many small rodents there are.
fields.confusions: The Common Kestrel also hovers, but it has reddish-brown feathers and a long tail. This one is mostly gray and white.
fields.anecdote: It can quickly make use of an area where rodents become plentiful.
fields.hint: Gray and white, I hang in the air above the fields.

fields.summary: A pale goose with a white head crossed by two black bands. Its bill and legs are orange.
fields.behaviour: She grazes on plants and looks for seeds in meadows and crops, often in a group.
fields.why_here: Bodies of water surrounded by grassy land can host the birds living free.
fields.migration: Native to Asia, it is seen in France mostly because of introductions or escapes. These birds do not necessarily follow the migration of wild populations.
fields.anecdote: In its natural range, it can cross very high mountains during migration.
fields.hint: My bill and feet are orange, and my head is white.

fields.summary: A big pale pink bird with long legs and a very long neck. Its curved bill lets it filter its food.
fields.behaviour: He stirs up the mud and filters the water with his bill turned upside down to catch tiny living things.
fields.why_here: Lagoons and shallow salty ponds give it food and quiet places to gather.
fields.migration: It lives all year in some French Mediterranean wetlands. Groups move between sites depending on food and conditions.
fields.confusions: The Chilean Flamingo has grayer legs with pink joints. Birds that escaped from captivity can make identification harder.
fields.anecdote: Its color comes from pigments found in its food.
fields.hint: I filter the water with my bill turned upside down.

fields.summary: A small streaky brown bird. Adults can have a reddish-brown throat and face during breeding. It likes to walk in short grass.
fields.behaviour: It mostly looks for small insects on the ground, moving among clumps and wet areas.
fields.why_here: Wet meadows, marsh edges and open ground are its rest stops.
fields.migration: It breeds in northern regions and crosses France during migration, but does not usually breed there.
fields.confusions: Without a visible reddish throat, it can look like the Meadow Pipit. Then the call and several feather details are needed.
fields.hint: In spring, my face can turn the color of brick.

fields.summary: A small beach bird with a sand-colored back. On each side of the chest, a dark patch makes a collar that does not close in the middle.
fields.behaviour: It runs on the sand, stops and pecks at small animals near the surface.
fields.why_here: Beaches, low dunes and open salt pans give it food and places to lay eggs right on the ground.
fields.migration: It nests on French coasts in the warm season. Some birds migrate, while others stay for the winter.
fields.confusions: The Common Ringed Plover has a full black collar. Here, the two dark patches stay apart on the chest.
fields.anecdote: Its nest is just a small scrape, so well hidden that you can walk right past it without seeing it.

fields.summary: A small water bird with pale wings. In summer, its black head and body contrast sharply with the white of the tail and upper wings.
fields.behaviour: She catches insects in flight or on the water's surface and also takes small water prey.
fields.why_here: Marshes and ponds rich in insects are its rest stops during its travels.
fields.migration: It winters in warmer regions and passes through France mostly in the warm season, during migration.
fields.confusions: In summer, the Black Tern has grayer wings and lacks the same contrast between the white shoulders and the black body.
fields.anecdote: Its much paler winter feathers make it harder to recognize than in summer.
fields.hint: In summer, my pale shoulders top a black body.

fields.summary: A brown bird of tall grass, with a slim body that lets it slip between the stems. You hear it far more often than you see it.
fields.behaviour: It walks under cover looking for insects and other small animals, and also some seeds.
fields.why_here: Tall meadows give it food and hiding places. Mowing late leaves time for the young to grow.
fields.migration: It comes back from Africa in spring and leaves after the warm season.
fields.by_ear: The male repeats a dry, two-part rasp, mostly at night, like a comb being rubbed.
fields.anecdote: Though it prefers walking and hiding, it makes a long migration by flying.
fields.hint: At night, my call rasps like a rubbed comb.

fields.summary: A stocky mountain bird with a streaky brown back and a gray head. Its pale throat is dotted with black and its sides are reddish-brown.
fields.behaviour: It looks for insects and seeds on the ground, between stones and on mountain meadows.
fields.why_here: Rocky slopes and piles of stones with a few plants give it food and shelter.
fields.migration: It stays in the French mountains all year, moving down to lower heights in winter.
fields.confusions: The Dunnock is smaller, without the same reddish-brown sides or the pale throat dotted with black.
fields.anecdote: It may look for food near mountain huts and visitors, while living in very harsh places.
fields.hint: My dotted throat explores the stones of the summits.

fields.summary: A diving duck with an angular head. The dark male has gray sides and pale marks on his bill.
fields.behaviour: He dives to take plants and small water animals.
fields.why_here: Ponds and lakes give it rest stops and feeding areas when it shows up in France.
fields.migration: Native to North America, it is a rare visitor in France, seen mostly in the cold season.
fields.confusions: The Tufted Duck has a crest and, on the male, white sides. The pale rings on the bill are a useful clue here.
fields.anecdote: The male's reddish-brown collar is much harder to see than the pale marks on his bill.
fields.hint: The dark male has gray sides and pale marks on his bill.

fields.summary: A small streaky brown bird of open spaces. Its bill turns yellow in the cold season.
fields.behaviour: She mostly looks for small seeds on the ground and in dry plants, often in a group.
fields.why_here: Wasteland, coastal meadows and open ground rich in seeds can welcome it in winter.
fields.migration: It nests mostly farther north and visits some French regions in the bad season.
fields.confusions: The male Common Linnet can have red on the forehead and chest. Here, the yellow bill in winter is a good clue.
fields.anecdote: She can stay grouped with other small seed-eating birds on ground full of dry plants.
fields.hint: My bill turns yellow when cold days come.

fields.summary: A brown bird covered with little white spots, with a long, strong bill. Its wings and tail are darker.
fields.behaviour: He cracks seeds and hazelnuts, then hides some of his stash in the ground.
fields.why_here: Mountain forests with pines, firs and hazel bushes give it food and shelter.
fields.migration: It usually stays put in its French regions. Some years, birds from other regions travel more.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are rough, loud and crackling, often repeated from a tree.
fields.confusions: The Common Starling is smaller and has a less massive bill. The sturdy shape helps tell them apart.
fields.anecdote: Seeds that were hidden and then forgotten can sprout and grow into new trees.
fields.hint: I bury seeds and sometimes plant trees by accident.

fields.summary: A seabird with pointed wings, with feathers that can be pale or dark. The adult has stretched-out central tail feathers.
fields.behaviour: It chases other seabirds to make them drop their food. It also catches small prey itself.
fields.why_here: Coastal waters rich in fishing birds can give it chances to feed.
fields.migration: It breeds in northern regions and passes mostly offshore from France during migration.
fields.confusions: The Pomarine Jaeger is bulkier. On a breeding adult, its long tail feathers end in a rounded tip rather than a pointed one.
fields.anecdote: A chase can force a fishing bird to drop its catch, which is grabbed right away in flight.
fields.hint: I chase winged fishers to take their meal.

fields.summary: A bird of prey with long, narrow wings that hunts close to the ground. The adult male is very pale, with small black tips on the wings.
fields.behaviour: It flies over open spaces to spot small mammals and birds.
fields.why_here: Meadows, crops and big open plains give it hunting grounds during its travels.
fields.migration: France is mostly on its migration routes. Sightings are mainly during spring and autumn migration.
fields.confusions: Females and young birds look like Montagu's and Hen Harriers. Telling them apart takes several details of the feathers and shape.
fields.hint: The male skims low over the fields on long, narrow wings.

fields.summary: A small dark water bird with a long tail and a short bill. Its shape looks slimmer than the big black fishers of the lakes.
fields.behaviour: It chases fish by diving and likes to rest on branches above the water.
fields.why_here: Marshes, lakes and rivers lined with plants give it fish, perches and shelter.
fields.migration: It is mostly found in southeastern Europe. Some birds scatter elsewhere, and France gets visitors.
fields.confusions: The Great Cormorant is much bigger, with a longer, stronger bill. Here, the small round head and long tail are useful.
fields.hint: Long-tailed dark fisher, I dry my wings on branches.

fields.summary: A brown goose with a long neck, orange legs and a bill mixing black and orange. It lives in big open spaces.
fields.behaviour: She grazes on plants and looks for seeds or plant leftovers in fields.
fields.why_here: Meadows and crops near quiet wetlands give it food and rest.
fields.migration: It comes from northern regions and can be seen in France in winter.
fields.confusions: The Tundra Bean Goose looks very much like it. The proportions of the head and bill matter, but a faraway view may not be enough.
fields.hint: Orange feet on the ground, I graze on winter plains.

fields.summary: A big, sturdy brown seabird with white marks in its wings. It looks powerful and agile above the waves.
fields.behaviour: It eats fish and other prey, picks up scraps, and sometimes chases other birds to steal their food.
fields.why_here: The sea gives it food. You can spot it from the coast when it passes close enough to shore.
fields.migration: It breeds in the North Atlantic and scatters widely at sea. It can be seen off the French coasts in different seasons.
fields.confusions: The Parasitic Jaeger is slimmer and has narrower wings. Here, the massive shape and the white wing marks help.
fields.anecdote: It can fiercely defend the area around its nest by diving at an intruder.
fields.hint: My broad brown wings carry two white flashes.

fields.summary: A rock bird whose male is slate blue. The female has duller brown feathers with fine patterns.
fields.behaviour: He watches for small animals from a rock or a roof, then drops to the ground to catch them.
fields.why_here: Cliffs, quarries, ruins and rocky villages give it perches, food and holes to nest in.
fields.migration: It lives all year in some French Mediterranean regions. Movements differ between populations.
fields.by_ear: Its song is melodious, with flute-like phrases, often sung from a very visible perch.
fields.confusions: The male Common Rock Thrush has an orange belly and a white patch on the back. Here, the male looks mostly dark blue.
fields.anecdote: The male's blue can look almost black when he is in the shade.
fields.hint: I perch on old roofs, then swoop down on prey.

fields.summary: A slender tern with long wings and a very forked tail. In summer, it has a black cap and a red bill.
fields.behaviour: She takes small fish and other animals near the surface, by diving or by snatching them in flight.
fields.why_here: Coastal waters give it fishing places during its journeys.
fields.migration: It breeds mostly in the north and passes offshore from France on its long trips to southern seas and back.
fields.confusions: The Common Tern looks very much like it. Compare the proportions of the bill, legs and tail, and the wings.
fields.anecdote: Its migrations take it between the Arctic and the seas near Antarctica.
fields.hint: In summer: black cap, red bill, deeply forked tail.

fields.summary: A big, very pale seabird. The adult has a pale gray back and white wingtips, without big black marks.
fields.behaviour: It takes fish, small animals and food scraps on coasts or at sea.
fields.why_here: Harbors, beaches and estuaries can host the few birds that reach France.
fields.migration: It breeds in the Arctic and shows up in France mostly in the cold season.
fields.confusions: The Iceland Gull is less bulky and has a thinner bill. Young birds need careful watching.
fields.anecdote: Even young birds have pale big wing feathers, which makes them look unusually pale.
fields.hint: My big pale wings have no black tips.

fields.summary: A black-and-white seabird with a thick, flat bill. It stands upright on rocks and flies fast, low over the water.
fields.behaviour: It dives to chase fish, using its wings underwater.
fields.why_here: Cliffs and rocky islets give it cracks to nest in. It feeds at sea.
fields.migration: It nests on a few French coasts and also visits French waters outside breeding. Birds scatter at sea after summer.
fields.confusions: The Common Murre has a thinner, pointed bill. The thick bill is a very useful clue here.
fields.anecdote: Despite its old name "little penguin" in French, this bird can fly, unlike the penguins of the Southern Hemisphere.
fields.hint: My thick bill goes with my dives under the waves.

fields.summary: A pale tern with a fairly short, sturdy black bill. Its wings are long and its cap turns black during breeding.
fields.behaviour: She catches big insects and small animals on the ground or near water, and does not depend only on fish.
fields.why_here: Lagoons and marshes near open land give it food and nesting sites.
fields.migration: It comes back in the warm season and leaves for warmer regions. In France, it is found mostly in some southern wetlands.
fields.confusions: The Sandwich Tern has a longer, thinner bill tipped with yellow. Here, the black bill is stubbier.
fields.anecdote: She can hunt over land, far from the line of the waves.
fields.hint: I also hunt big insects far from the waves.

fields.summary: A bird with a green back and a gray head. The male has a small red patch on the forehead.
fields.behaviour: It eats a lot of ants, which it looks for on the ground and in wood. It also searches trees for small animals.
fields.why_here: Leafy or mixed forests with old trees and clearings give it food and holes.
fields.migration: It mostly stays put in its French regions.
fields.by_ear: Its song is a series of whistled notes that slow down and often drop toward the end.
fields.confusions: The European Green Woodpecker has more red on the head and a wider black mask. Here, the head is mostly gray.
fields.anecdote: A long, sticky tongue helps it pull ants out of their tunnels.
fields.hint: My long sticky tongue fetches ants from their tunnels.

fields.summary: A small goose with very contrasting black, white and reddish-brown patterns. Its chest and part of its cheek are reddish-brown.
fields.behaviour: She grazes on grasses and eats plants in meadows and crops, often with other geese.
fields.why_here: Open ground near quiet resting places can welcome the rare visitors.
fields.migration: It nests in the Siberian Arctic. France mostly gets rare winter visitors, and some birds may also come from captivity.
fields.anecdote: Its bright colors are less easy to make out from far away, especially in a big flock.
fields.hint: My bold black, white and rusty pattern stands out among other geese.

fields.summary: A big goose with a long neck, a dark nape and a pale throat. The bill of the wild form is dark.
fields.behaviour: It mostly eats plants, grazing on banks and grassy ground.
fields.why_here: Bodies of water and meadows can host birds that come from farms or introductions.
fields.migration: The wild species is Asian. In France, sightings are mostly of farm or escaped birds, with no regular natural migration calendar.
fields.anecdote: Some farm geese with a big bump above the bill come from this species.
fields.hint: My dark nape follows my long pale neck.

fields.summary: A small insect-eating bird. The male in breeding plumage is black and white, with a full white collar around his neck.
fields.behaviour: He watches from a branch, darts out to catch an insect, then often goes back to a perch.
fields.why_here: Leafy forests with old hollow trees give it holes to nest in.
fields.migration: It comes back from Africa in spring and leaves after breeding. In France, it nests mostly in some eastern regions.
fields.confusions: The male European Pied Flycatcher does not have the same full white collar. Females are much harder to tell apart.
fields.anecdote: It can use a nest box when natural holes are poor or missing.

fields.summary: A small falcon of warm regions. The male has a reddish-brown back without big spots, and a gray head.
fields.behaviour: He mostly hunts big insects in open spaces, in flight or on the ground. He can feed in a group.
fields.why_here: Dry meadows, crops and open land near buildings or cliffs give it food and holes to nest in.
fields.migration: It comes back from Africa in the warm season. In France, it nests mostly in some southern areas, then leaves after summer.
fields.by_ear: Its cries are short and repeated, especially around the colonies.
fields.confusions: The male Common Kestrel has a clearly spotted back. Females of the two species are much harder to tell apart.
fields.anecdote: Several pairs can nest side by side in the same group of buildings or rocks.
fields.hint: The male has a reddish-brown back without big spots.

fields.summary: A small sea gull with very contrasting wing patterns. In flight, white and black triangles stand out against the gray top.
fields.behaviour: She takes small animals from the water's surface and often feeds far out at sea.
fields.why_here: The open sea gives it food. When it passes close to the coast, you can sometimes see it from land.
fields.migration: It nests in the Arctic and passes mostly offshore from France during migration, especially after summer.
fields.confusions: The triangle pattern of black, white and gray on the wings helps tell it from other small gulls.
fields.anecdote: Its slightly forked tail completes a very elegant shape in flight.
fields.hint: My wings draw black, white and gray triangles.

fields.summary: A big streaky brown pipit with long legs. It often stands upright to look over the grass.
fields.behaviour: It walks on the ground and mostly catches small insects between the clumps.
fields.why_here: Meadows, wasteland and open grassy ground can give it a rest stop or a winter home.
fields.migration: It nests in Asia and shows up in France mostly in autumn. Some birds stay for the winter.
fields.confusions: The Tawny Pipit is more evenly pale. The posture, the chest marks and the call help tell them apart.
fields.hint: Standing on my long legs, I rise above the grass.

fields.summary: A seabird dark brown above and paler below, often with brownish sides. It glides close to the waves on narrow wings.
fields.behaviour: It takes fish and other sea prey by diving or from the surface. It can gather where food is plentiful.
fields.why_here: It feeds at sea, sometimes near French coasts, in areas rich in fish.
fields.migration: It nests in the Balearic Islands. After breeding, many birds head into the Atlantic and visit French waters.
fields.confusions: The Manx Shearwater usually shows a sharper black-and-white contrast. Light and distance can make the comparison hard.
fields.anecdote: It comes ashore to nest, but spends most of its life at sea.
fields.hint: I glide just above the waves on long dark wings.

fields.summary: A small brown bird with pale eyebrows. A yellow spot, sometimes hidden, colors its throat.
fields.behaviour: It picks up seeds on the ground and also catches insects, especially to feed its chicks.
fields.why_here: It lives in dry, rocky landscapes. Holes in old walls and trees can shelter its nest.
fields.migration: It usually stays in the regions where it lives, with local movements.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are nasal, fairly loud and often repeated.
fields.confusions: The House Sparrow has no yellow spot on the throat and no pale pattern on the head like this one.
fields.anecdote: Its small yellow spot can vanish under the nearby feathers when it keeps its head down.
fields.hint: A little yellow jewel hides under my bill.

fields.summary: The Western Subalpine Warbler slips through Mediterranean bushes. The male has a reddish-brown chest and a thin white mustache.
fields.behaviour: She looks for small insects among leaves and twigs.
fields.why_here: Dry shrubland and thick scrub give it food and hiding places.
fields.migration: A migrant, it comes back in spring and spends the winter in Africa.
fields.confusions: Other small warblers with a white mustache look very much like it. Good watching and listening are needed.
fields.hint: My white mustache stands out on my reddish chest.

fields.summary: The Pallid Swift spends much of its life in flight. Its brown feathers contrast only a little with its pale throat.
fields.behaviour: It catches insects in the open sky and likes to gather with its neighbors.
fields.why_here: It nests in holes in cliffs or buildings, mostly in regions with a mild climate.
fields.migration: A migrant, it visits France in the warm season, then winters in Africa.
fields.by_ear: It gives piercing screams in flight, especially around nesting sites.
fields.confusions: The Common Swift is very similar. Color alone is not enough, because the light changes their look a lot.
fields.anecdote: Its short legs are mostly used to cling to walls near the nest.
fields.hint: I chase insects without leaving the sky.

fields.summary: The European Storm Petrel is a tiny dark seabird with a white rump. It seems to brush the waves.
fields.behaviour: It picks small prey from the sea surface, sometimes with its feet resting on the water.
fields.why_here: It lives far out at sea and goes to small islands to nest in holes.
fields.migration: Its travels take it far from the colonies. It can be seen off the French coasts.
fields.confusions: Leach's Storm Petrel has a forked tail. This one's tail is more square.
fields.anecdote: It often goes to its nest at night, when gulls are less likely to spot it.
fields.hint: A small dark butterfly, I brush the waves.

fields.summary: The Ruddy Duck is a stocky duck whose tail can stand up. In breeding feathers, the male has a reddish-brown body and a blue bill.
fields.behaviour: She dives to look for food in the water and in the mud.
fields.why_here: It lives on bodies of water with plenty of plants along the shore.
fields.migration: Native to the Americas, it was brought to Europe by people. Its local movements are not a regular migration to France.
fields.confusions: The male White-headed Duck has a much whiter head and a bill that swells strongly at the base.
fields.anecdote: The male's bill turns blue during breeding.
fields.hint: My cocked tail often sticks out of the water.

fields.summary: The Pomarine Jaeger is a powerful seabird. The adult in breeding feathers has widened, twisted central tail feathers.
fields.behaviour: At sea, it chases other birds to make them drop their food. It also hunts prey directly.
fields.why_here: It lives out at sea and breeds on the Arctic tundra.
fields.migration: A migrant, it can pass offshore from France on its trips between the Arctic and its ocean homes.
fields.confusions: The Parasitic Jaeger is usually slimmer and does not have the same long spoon-shaped tail feathers.
fields.anecdote: On the tundra, lemmings make up an important part of its diet.
fields.hint: In summer, my tail carries curious spoons.

fields.summary: The Iceland Gull is a big, very pale seabird. Its wings usually lack the black tips of the familiar gulls.
fields.behaviour: It looks for fish and other small prey, and also picks up scraps.
fields.why_here: Harbors and coasts can welcome the rare visitors from the north.
fields.migration: It nests in Arctic regions. In France, it is mostly a rare winter visitor.
fields.confusions: The Glaucous Gull is bulkier, with a more powerful bill.
fields.hint: My big pale wings look painted without any black.

fields.summary: The male Common Rock Thrush combines a blue-gray head, an orange belly and a white patch on the back. The female is brown and speckled.
fields.behaviour: He watches the ground from a rock, then pounces on insects.
fields.why_here: It looks for open, stony slopes, where rocks alternate with low plants.
fields.migration: A migrant, it comes in the warm season and spends the winter in Africa.
fields.by_ear: Its song is melodious, made of flute-like phrases.
fields.confusions: The male Blue Rock Thrush has neither an orange belly nor a white patch on the back.
fields.anecdote: The male can sing during a short display flight.
fields.hint: Blue above and orange below, I leap on insects.

fields.summary: The Greater Short-toed Lark is a small brown bird of open, dry land, with a lightly marked chest.
fields.behaviour: She walks on the ground looking for seeds and small insects.
fields.why_here: She likes bare ground, dry grassland and some thin crops.
fields.migration: A migrant, it is mostly here in the warm season and winters mainly in Africa.
fields.by_ear: She sings in flight over her territory.
fields.confusions: The Eurasian Skylark has a more clearly streaked chest and a different shape. Small larks need careful watching.
fields.anecdote: Its plain feathers make it hard to find again when it lands on bare earth.
fields.hint: My song falls from the sky onto dry ground.

fields.summary: The Common Murre is a seabird, dark above and white below. It stands almost upright on cliff ledges.
fields.behaviour: It chases fish underwater, using its wings like flippers.
fields.why_here: It nests in colonies on coastal cliffs and feeds at sea.
fields.migration: Found at sea around France, it scatters after breeding. Birds from the north also come into our waters.
fields.confusions: The Razorbill has a much thicker bill. The Common Murre's bill is long and pointed.
fields.anecdote: Its egg is laid right on the rock, with no built nest.
fields.hint: My wings carry me through the air and underwater.

fields.summary: The European Rock Pipit is a small olive-brown bird of rocky shores. Its chest is marked with dark streaks.
fields.behaviour: It walks among stones and washed-up seaweed to catch small animals.
fields.why_here: Rocky coasts give it hiding places and food renewed by the tides.
fields.migration: Some stay near their breeding coasts. Others come down from northern Europe for the winter.
fields.confusions: The Water Pipit is often more contrasting, but winter feathers can be hard to tell apart.
fields.anecdote: It explores heaps of seaweed where many small animals without backbones hide.
fields.hint: I trot among the seaweed at the edge of the waves.

fields.summary: The African Sacred Ibis is a big white bird with a black head and neck. Its long curved bill probes wet areas.
fields.behaviour: It looks for small animals in the mud and can also make use of food scraps.
fields.why_here: It lives in marshes, wet meadows and along banks. In Europe, it is here because of introductions.
fields.migration: Native mainly to Africa, it does not follow a natural seasonal migration in France like the regular wild visitors.
fields.confusions: The Little Egret has a straight bill, a feathered neck and a slimmer shape.
fields.anecdote: In ancient Egypt, this bird was linked to the god Thoth.
fields.hint: My long curved bill continues a bare head.

fields.summary: The Spotless Starling is a dark bird with a glossy shine, found mostly around the western Mediterranean.
fields.behaviour: It digs in the ground for small animals without backbones and also eats fruit.
fields.why_here: It lives in villages, crops and open land with holes to nest in.
fields.migration: It mostly stays put, with local movements.
fields.by_ear: Its repertoire mixes whistles, creaky notes and imitations.
fields.confusions: The Common Starling has bolder pale spots, especially in fresh feathers. Young birds are harder to tell apart.
fields.anecdote: It can imitate sounds it hears around it.
fields.hint: My dark suit shines in the Mediterranean sun.

fields.summary: The Manx Shearwater is a seabird, black above and white below. It zips close to the waves on narrow wings.
fields.behaviour: It catches small fish by diving and can gather around schools of prey.
fields.why_here: It lives at sea and nests in burrows or holes on islands.
fields.migration: A great traveler of the Atlantic, it roams widely outside breeding. Birds visit French waters in different seasons.
fields.confusions: The Yelkouan Shearwater looks very much like it. The place of the sighting and the feather details must be checked together.
fields.anecdote: At colonies, it usually goes to its burrow in the dark.
fields.hint: Black back, white belly, I skim the swell.

fields.summary: The Lapland Longspur is a small bird of northern lands. In winter, its streaky brown feathers hide it on the ground.
fields.behaviour: It looks for seeds on the ground and catches insects during breeding.
fields.why_here: In winter, it visits open coastal areas and bare fields.
fields.migration: It nests in the far north. A few birds winter in France, mostly near the coast.
fields.confusions: The Common Reed Bunting often lives in leafier places. A careful look at the head and wings helps tell them apart.
fields.anecdote: The male looks very different in summer, with a mostly black head and chest.
fields.hint: In winter, my stripes hide me in the fields.

fields.summary: The Horned Lark wears a black and yellow mask. Small feathers standing up on its head sometimes look like two horns.
fields.behaviour: She looks for seeds and small animals without backbones, walking on the ground.
fields.why_here: The few French visitors mostly use open coastal areas.
fields.migration: Birds from the north come to spend the winter on the coasts of western Europe, including France.
fields.confusions: Its colorful mask and little horns set it apart from the larks usually met in France.
fields.anecdote: Its horns are feathers, not bony growths.
fields.hint: My black-and-yellow mask hides little tufts of feathers on my head.

fields.summary: The male Black Grouse is dark, with red marks above the eyes and a curled tail. The brown female blends in with the plants.
fields.behaviour: He eats buds, leaves and berries. Males gather to display.
fields.why_here: It lives on heaths and open land near the upper edge of mountain forests.
fields.migration: It stays in its mountain ranges, with local movements through the seasons.
fields.by_ear: Males make deep cooing sounds mixed with hissing during displays.
fields.confusions: The Western Capercaillie is much bulkier and lives more in the forest.
fields.anecdote: In winter, it can shelter in the snow to keep warm.
fields.hint: My tail draws a lyre when I display.

fields.summary: The Sooty Shearwater is an all-dark seabird with long wings. The underside of the wings often shows a paler patch.
fields.behaviour: It dives to catch fish and other sea animals.
fields.why_here: It lives far out and can come close to the coast when conditions bring its food together.
fields.migration: Nesting in the Southern Hemisphere, it makes great ocean journeys. It passes through French waters, especially after our summer.
fields.confusions: The other shearwaters common off France usually have a pale belly.
fields.anecdote: Its journey takes it between the two hemispheres.
fields.hint: An all-dark traveler, I cross the oceans.

fields.summary: The Northern Fulmar looks like a gull with a thick neck, but it flies on stiff wings. Its bill has tubes you can see.
fields.behaviour: It takes fish, small sea animals and scraps from the water's surface.
fields.why_here: It nests on cliffs and spends a lot of time far out at sea.
fields.migration: It stays in the seas of northern Europe all year and spreads out widely after breeding.
fields.confusions: Gulls usually flap their wings more and do not have tubes on the bill.
fields.anecdote: To defend itself, the young bird can spit out an oily, smelly liquid.
fields.hint: My bill has tubes above the nostrils.

fields.summary: Scopoli's Shearwater is a big seabird with a gray-brown back, a white belly and a yellow bill.
fields.behaviour: It switches between flaps and long glides over the waves to look for fish and squid.
fields.why_here: It nests on Mediterranean islands and feeds at sea.
fields.migration: It goes to the Mediterranean to breed, then heads into the Atlantic after the warm season.
fields.confusions: Cory's Shearwater looks extremely similar. Telling them apart takes a careful look at the underside of the wingtips.
fields.hint: I glide over the waves with my yellow bill.

fields.summary: The Purple Sandpiper is a small, stocky, dark bird of rocky coasts. The base of its bill and its legs are yellowish.
fields.behaviour: It catches small animals without backbones among the seaweed and the stones beaten by the waves.
fields.why_here: It looks for coastal rocks, sea walls and piers.
fields.migration: Nesting in northern regions, it stays in France mostly outside the breeding season.
fields.confusions: The Dunlin more often visits mudflats and has dark legs.
fields.anecdote: It can feed very close to the waves that regularly cover the rocks.
fields.hint: I look for my meal on splashed rocks.

fields.summary: The Pectoral Sandpiper has a finely streaked chest that contrasts sharply with its white belly.
fields.behaviour: It probes the mud and catches small animals without backbones in shallow areas.
fields.why_here: Marshes and muddy banks give it rest stops during its travels.
fields.migration: It nests in the Arctic and rarely shows up in France during migration, mostly in autumn.
fields.confusions: The streaks on its chest stop fairly abruptly above the white belly, unlike several small sandpipers.
fields.hint: Fine streaks end sharply where my white belly begins.

fields.summary: The Iberian Chiffchaff is a small bird, greenish-brown above and pale below. Its song helps more than its feathers to recognize it.
fields.behaviour: It catches small insects in leaves and branches.
fields.why_here: It lives in woods and shrubby areas, especially in southwestern France.
fields.migration: A migrant, it comes back in spring and spends the winter in Africa.
fields.by_ear: Its song combines repeated notes and a faster part, different from the steady swing of the Common Chiffchaff.
fields.confusions: The Common Chiffchaff looks extremely close to the eye. Hearing a full song is very valuable.
fields.hint: My song reveals what my feathers hide.

fields.summary: The Eurasian Pygmy Owl is a very small owl with a round head and yellow eyes. It lives mostly in mountain forests in France.
fields.behaviour: She catches small mammals and birds, sometimes in broad daylight.
fields.why_here: She uses tree holes, often dug earlier by woodpeckers.
fields.migration: It usually stays in the regions where it lives, with local movements.
fields.by_ear: Its song is a series of simple whistles, spaced apart and fairly pure.
fields.confusions: The Boreal Owl is bigger and has a more clearly outlined face disc.
fields.anecdote: She can store prey in holes to eat later.
fields.hint: I stash my food in tree holes and sometimes hunt in daylight.

fields.summary: The Egyptian Vulture is a pale vulture with black-edged wings. The adult has a yellow face with no feathers.
fields.behaviour: It eats animal leftovers and also takes advantage of small prey.
fields.why_here: It looks for open landscapes near the cliffs where it builds its nest.
fields.migration: French nesters come back in spring and spend the winter in Africa.
fields.confusions: The other vultures in France are bigger and do not have its white feathers contrasting with black.
fields.anecdote: It knows how to use a stone to break big eggs, a behavior seen in Africa.
fields.hint: My yellow face contrasts with my big pale wings.

fields.summary: The Atlantic Puffin is a black-and-white seabird with a brightly colored bill during breeding. It nests on some islands of Brittany.
fields.behaviour: It dives to catch small fish and uses its wings to move underwater.
fields.why_here: It nests in a burrow on islands and looks for food at sea.
fields.migration: After breeding, it leaves the colonies and spreads out over the Atlantic.
fields.confusions: The Razorbill has neither its white face nor its big colorful bill.
fields.anecdote: It can carry several fish lined up in its bill to feed its chick.
fields.hint: My colorful bill carries several fish at once.

fields.summary: The Snow Goose is a North American goose, often white with black wingtips. There is also a form with a dark body and a white head.
fields.behaviour: She grazes on plants and looks for roots or seeds on the ground.
fields.why_here: The few birds seen visit wetlands, meadows and crops.
fields.migration: A migrant in North America, it stays rare in France. Some birds may come from captivity.
fields.confusions: Ross's Goose is smaller, with a shorter, more compact bill.
fields.anecdote: White birds and dark birds can belong to the same species.
fields.hint: White or dark, my head stays pale as an adult.

fields.summary: The Iberian Grey Shrike is gray, white and black, with a dark band over the eyes and a hooked bill.
fields.behaviour: She watches from a bush or a wire, then catches big insects and small animals with backbones.
fields.why_here: It lives in dry, open southern landscapes dotted with bushes.
fields.migration: It mostly stays put, with local movements.
fields.confusions: The Great Grey Shrike looks very much like it. The shade of the underside and the place help, but are not always enough.
fields.anecdote: She can stick prey on thorns to keep them or tear them apart.
fields.hint: My pantry may be hung on thorns.

fields.summary: The Long-tailed Jaeger is a slender seabird. The adult in breeding feathers has very long central tail feathers.
fields.behaviour: It catches small prey and can chase other seabirds to take their food.
fields.why_here: It nests on the tundra and spends the rest of the year at sea.
fields.migration: A long-distance migrant, it is mostly seen passing offshore from France.
fields.confusions: Young jaegers look very much alike. The long tail feathers are mostly useful to recognize adults in breeding feathers.

fields.summary: The male Indian Peafowl has a shiny blue neck and a huge train decorated with eye-shaped spots. The female is plainer.
fields.behaviour: He walks on the ground to eat seeds, fruit and small animals, then perches to sleep.
fields.why_here: Native to Asia, it is mostly met in parks and farms in France.
fields.migration: It does not migrate seasonally to France. The birds here come from captivity.
fields.by_ear: Its powerful call sounds like a long, whiny scream, often written "leon".
fields.anecdote: The male's big wheel is made mostly of feathers above the true tail.
fields.hint: I spread a wheel covered with colored eyes.

fields.summary: The male Italian Sparrow has a chestnut cap, pale cheeks and a black bib. He looks very much like the other village sparrows.
fields.behaviour: He mostly eats seeds and feeds his chicks with insects.
fields.why_here: It lives in villages and farmland, especially around Italy and Corsica.
fields.migration: It mostly stays put.
fields.by_ear: It makes short chirps, close to those of other sparrows.
fields.confusions: The male House Sparrow has a gray top of the head. Females are much harder to tell apart.
fields.hint: My chestnut cap tops pale cheeks.

fields.summary: The Great Spotted Cuckoo is a slim bird with a long tail and a small crest. Its dark back has pale spots.
fields.behaviour: It eats caterpillars, including some hairy ones.
fields.why_here: It lives in open landscapes with trees, especially in Mediterranean regions.
fields.migration: In France, it is present mostly in spring and summer. It winters mainly in Africa.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are rough, fast and loud.
fields.confusions: The Common Cuckoo has neither its small crest nor its back dotted with white.
fields.anecdote: The female lays in other birds' nests, especially magpies' nests, which then raise her chick.
fields.hint: Other parents raise my chick in their nest.

fields.summary: The Ringed Teal is a small South American duck. The male has a black mark on the top of the head and the neck.
fields.behaviour: It feeds in shallow water and can perch in trees.
fields.why_here: In its home range, it lives in wooded wetlands. In France, sightings are of birds from captivity.
fields.migration: This species has no regular natural migration to France.
fields.anecdote: Unlike many familiar ducks, it readily uses branches as perches.
fields.hint: I can perch above my pond.

fields.summary: The Iberian Green Woodpecker is a green bird with a red cap. It is very close to the European Green Woodpecker. It lives mostly in the Iberian Peninsula.
fields.behaviour: It loves to look for ants on the ground and catches them with its long tongue.
fields.why_here: It likes open woods and landscapes with a mix of trees and open spaces.
fields.migration: It mostly stays in one place, especially in the north of its range near the Pyrenees.
fields.confusions: The European Green Woodpecker has more black around the eye. You need a good view of the head to tell them apart.
fields.hint: I probe anthills with my long tongue.

fields.summary: The Citril Finch is a small yellow-green bird with a grey neck. It lives in the mountains of south-west Europe.
fields.behaviour: It looks mostly for seeds, on plants and on the ground.
fields.why_here: It likes light conifer forests close to mountain meadows.
fields.migration: It moves with the seasons and may come down to places with less snow in winter.
fields.confusions: The male Eurasian Siskin has a black cap. The Citril Finch does not.
fields.hint: My grey neck goes with yellow and green clothes.

fields.summary: The Red-necked Phalarope is a small water bird with a thin bill. Unlike many of its relatives, it loves to swim.
fields.behaviour: It catches tiny animals on the water's surface, sometimes by spinning around on itself.
fields.why_here: It stops over on calm bodies of water and spends part of the year at sea.
fields.migration: It breeds in the far north and appears in France mostly during migration.
fields.confusions: The Grey Phalarope has a sturdier bill. Their feathers change a lot with the season.
fields.anecdote: In this species, the male sits on the eggs and looks after the chicks.
fields.hint: I spin on the water to bring my meal up.

fields.summary: The Great Shearwater is a big brown and white seabird. Its dark cap and pale collar give it a striking head.
fields.behaviour: It hunts fish and squid, which it grabs at the surface or by diving.
fields.why_here: It lives out over the Atlantic and can gather where food is plentiful.
fields.migration: It breeds in the South Atlantic and flies north to the North Atlantic during our summer.
fields.confusions: Large shearwaters with a yellow bill do not have its dark bill or the same bold head pattern.
fields.anecdote: The breeding seasons of its southern colonies are the opposite of those of our own nesting birds.
fields.hint: My dark cap stands out against a pale collar.

fields.summary: The Little Crake is a small marsh bird that often stays hidden. The male has a bluish-grey belly.
fields.behaviour: It catches small invertebrates, animals without a backbone, as it walks over plants and along the banks.
fields.why_here: It looks for marshes full of reeds and water plants.
fields.migration: It is a migrant and is rarely seen in France, mostly when passing through.
fields.confusions: The Baillon's Crake is very similar. You need to look carefully at the flanks, the bill and the shape.
fields.hint: In the reeds, my steps often go unseen.

fields.summary: The Bearded Vulture is a big vulture with narrow wings and a diamond-shaped tail. Black feathers hang under its bill like a beard.
fields.behaviour: It eats mostly bones, which it may drop onto rocks to break them.
fields.why_here: It lives in rocky mountains and nests on cliffs.
fields.migration: Adults usually stay in their own mountain range. Young birds can travel long distances.
fields.confusions: The other vultures of France have a shorter tail that is less clearly diamond-shaped.
fields.anecdote: It colours its pale feathers by bathing in water or soil rich in iron.
fields.hint: I break bones by dropping them on rocks.

fields.summary: The Alpine Chough is a black mountain bird with a yellow bill and red legs. It flies with great ease.
fields.behaviour: It eats insects, fruit and seeds, and sometimes takes leftovers near mountain huts.
fields.why_here: It lives on cliffs and high meadows, often in groups.
fields.migration: It stays in the mountains and may come lower down when snow covers its food.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are high and whistling, often given in flight.
fields.confusions: The Red-billed Chough has a longer, curved, red bill.
fields.anecdote: It uses the moving air along cliffs to perform acrobatics.

fields.summary: The Marsh Sandpiper is a slim, elegant water bird with long legs and a very thin bill.
fields.behaviour: It catches small animals as it walks through shallow water.
fields.why_here: It looks for marshes and bodies of water with open banks.
fields.migration: It is a migrant and a rare visitor to France, mostly during its seasonal journeys.
fields.confusions: The Common Greenshank is sturdier and has a thicker bill that curves slightly upward.
fields.hint: My bill looks as thin as a needle.

fields.summary: The Long-legged Buzzard is a large bird of prey of open country. Its feathers vary a lot, often with reddish tones.
fields.behaviour: It hunts small mammals and other animals, from a perch or in flight.
fields.why_here: It lives mostly in dry, open landscapes.
fields.migration: Its populations move in different ways. In France, it remains a rare visitor.
fields.confusions: The Common Buzzard can look very similar. Reddish colour alone is not enough to identify it.
fields.hint: From a high perch, I scan dry ground.

fields.summary: Cory's Shearwater is a big seabird, grey-brown above and white below. Its yellow bill is easy to see up close.
fields.behaviour: It flies close to the waves and catches fish or squid at sea.
fields.why_here: It nests on Atlantic islands and looks for food far out at sea.
fields.migration: It travels widely across the Atlantic. French waters are visited mostly in summer and during passages.
fields.confusions: The Scopoli's Shearwater looks almost exactly the same. Details of the underwing matter.
fields.hint: My yellow bill goes with long glides over the sea.

fields.summary: The Monk Parakeet is a green bird with a grey face and chest. It comes from South America and also lives in some European cities.
fields.behaviour: It moves in noisy groups and eats seeds, fruit and other plants.
fields.why_here: Parks and big city trees give it food and places to build its nests.
fields.migration: Introduced birds usually stay in their area, with short local moves.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are harsh, chatty and repeated.
fields.confusions: The Rose-ringed Parakeet has no grey chest and has a longer, thinner tail.
fields.anecdote: It builds huge stick nests that can hold several couples, each in its own room.
fields.hint: Together we build a stick house with many rooms.

fields.summary: The Boreal Owl is a small owl with a big head and yellow eyes. Its pale face is clearly framed in dark.
fields.behaviour: It hunts mostly small rodents at night.
fields.why_here: It lives in forests, often in the mountains, and nests in tree holes.
fields.migration: Some birds stay put, while others move depending on how many prey there are.
fields.by_ear: Its song is a steady string of small hollow notes, repeated in series.
fields.confusions: The Eurasian Pygmy Owl is smaller and its face is less clearly framed.
fields.anecdote: Old holes made by the Black Woodpecker can be used as its home.
fields.hint: An old hole of a big woodpecker becomes my bedroom.

fields.summary: Leach's Storm Petrel is a small dark seabird with a white rump and a forked tail.
fields.behaviour: It catches small prey near the surface, fluttering above the waves.
fields.why_here: It lives out at sea and breeds in burrows on islands.
fields.migration: It travels across the Atlantic and can be seen off France, especially during autumn journeys.
fields.confusions: The European Storm Petrel is smaller and has no clearly forked tail.
fields.hint: My small forked tail sways above the waves.

fields.summary: The Little Auk is a tiny, chubby black and white seabird with a very short bill.
fields.behaviour: It dives and catches mostly small sea crustaceans.
fields.why_here: It nests in rock piles in Arctic regions and spends the winter at sea.
fields.migration: Some birds move down the North Atlantic in winter. They sometimes reach French coasts, especially after storms.
fields.confusions: The Common Murre and the Razorbill are much bigger, with a larger bill.
fields.anecdote: Like other seabirds of its family, it uses its wings to swim underwater.
fields.hint: Black-and-white diver, I have a very short bill.

fields.summary: The Cinereous Vulture is a huge, dark bird of prey with broad wings. It soars for a long time over open country.
fields.behaviour: It feeds on dead animals, and its strong bill can tear their tough parts.
fields.why_here: It needs wide open spaces to feed and big trees to nest in.
fields.migration: Adults usually stay close to their home area. Young birds may wander far from the colonies.
fields.confusions: The Griffon Vulture is paler and looks more contrasted, with a longer neck.
fields.anecdote: Unlike the Griffon Vulture, it builds its nest in a tree.
fields.hint: Big dark glider, I build my nest in a tree.

fields.summary: The Western Orphean Warbler is a big warbler with a pale belly. The male has a dark cap that makes his pale eye stand out.
fields.behaviour: It looks for insects in the leaves and also eats fruit.
fields.why_here: It likes open woods and Mediterranean landscapes full of shrubs.
fields.migration: It is a migrant. It comes back in summer and spends the winter in Africa.
fields.by_ear: Its song is loud, with flute-like notes and rougher parts.
fields.confusions: The Eurasian Blackcap is smaller and has a dark eye.
fields.hint: My pale eye stands out under a dark cap.

fields.summary: The adult male Common Rosefinch has red on his head and chest. Females and young birds are brownish with streaks.
fields.behaviour: It eats seeds, buds and small invertebrates, animals without a backbone.
fields.why_here: It lives in bushes and along woodland edges, often near wet areas.
fields.migration: It is a migrant and appears mostly in summer in Europe. It is not often seen in France.
fields.by_ear: The male sings a short, clear, musical whistled phrase.
fields.confusions: The male Common Linnet has red too, but the pattern on his head and chest is different.
fields.anecdote: Young males do not get the bright red of the adults right away.
fields.hint: My whistled song goes with a red chest in adults.

fields.summary: The Western Black-eared Wheatear is a small bird of open Mediterranean country. The male has pale feathers that contrast with black wings and face marks.
fields.behaviour: It spots insects from a rock or a bush, then drops down to catch them.
fields.why_here: It likes dry, stony, sunny ground with little plant cover.
fields.migration: It is a migrant. It visits the south of France in summer and spends the winter in Africa.
fields.confusions: The Eastern Black-eared Wheatear is extremely similar. Females and young birds are especially hard to tell apart.
fields.anecdote: Some males have a black throat, others a pale one.
fields.hint: I watch the warm stones from my little perch.

fields.summary: Bonelli's Eagle is a powerful bird of prey of Mediterranean regions. The adult has a pale belly marked with fine dark spots.
fields.behaviour: It hunts birds and rabbits, in flight or from a lookout post.
fields.why_here: It looks for open country to hunt and quiet cliffs to nest on.
fields.migration: Adults stay in one place all year. Young birds sometimes spread far from where they were born.
fields.confusions: The Golden Eagle is bigger and has pale areas in different places on its feathers.
fields.anecdote: Both birds of a pair can hunt together.
fields.hint: As a pair, we watch over the scrubland from the cliffs.

fields.summary: Wilson's Storm Petrel is a tiny dark seabird with a white band on its rump and long legs.
fields.behaviour: It catches tiny animals near the surface, flapping its wings and sometimes touching the water with its feet.
fields.why_here: It lives far out at sea, where currents gather its food.
fields.migration: It breeds in the Southern Hemisphere, flies north to the North Atlantic in our summer and can reach French waters.
fields.confusions: The European Storm Petrel has legs that stick out less behind the tail and a different pattern under the wings.
fields.anecdote: Its long journeys take it from one half of the world to the other.
fields.hint: My feet seem to walk on the waves.

fields.summary: Audouin's Gull is a pale seabird with a dark red bill marked with black. It belongs to the Mediterranean.
fields.behaviour: It fishes for small fish and also uses food made easy to reach by fishing boats.
fields.why_here: It lives along the coast and nests in colonies, often on small islands.
fields.migration: After breeding, some birds leave the colonies and move to other Mediterranean or Atlantic coasts.
fields.confusions: The Yellow-legged Gull has a heavier yellow bill and yellow legs. An adult Audouin's Gull has different ones.
fields.hint: My dark red bill goes with my pale grey suit.

fields.summary: The Ring-billed Gull is a North American bird with a pale grey back. The adult has a black ring near the tip of its yellow bill.
fields.behaviour: It eats fish, small animals and food scraps.
fields.why_here: The few visitors come to coasts, harbours and bodies of water.
fields.migration: It is a rare visitor to France, seen mostly outside the breeding season.
fields.confusions: The Mew Gull looks similar but usually has a thinner bill. The ring on the bill alone is not enough to identify it.
fields.hint: A rare visitor from North America, I have a pale grey back.

fields.summary: The Red-breasted Flycatcher is a small woodland bird with big dark eyes. The adult male may have an orange throat.
fields.behaviour: It catches insects from a perch and also hunts them among the leaves.
fields.why_here: It uses woods and bushy places when it stops during its journey.
fields.migration: It is a migrant, and mostly a rare passing visitor in France, especially in autumn.
fields.confusions: The European Robin is chubbier and its orange spreads more over the face and chest.
fields.anecdote: White marks on the sides of its tail show when it spreads it open.
fields.hint: My half-open tail shows little white windows.

fields.summary: The African Stonechat is a small African bird that likes to sit in plain view on a perch. Males show black, white and orange-brown contrasts.
fields.behaviour: It watches for insects from a stem or a bush, then dashes out to catch them.
fields.why_here: It lives in open places where plants give it lookout posts.
fields.confusions: Other stonechats can look very much like it. A photo alone cannot always settle it.
fields.hint: I watch for insects from the top of a stem.

fields.summary: The Great Bustard is a very big ground bird of the plains. The male has a reddish chest and long feathers near the bill.
fields.behaviour: It walks along looking for plants and small animals.
fields.why_here: It needs wide open plains with few disturbances.
fields.migration: Populations move in different ways depending on where they live. In France, it is a very rare sight.
fields.confusions: The Little Bustard is much smaller and does not have the same heavy look.
fields.anecdote: During his display, the male puffs up his neck and flips his feathers over to show lots of white.
fields.hint: In display, my feathers turn me into a white ball.

fields.summary: The Lesser White-fronted Goose is a small grey goose with a white forehead and a yellow ring around the eye.
fields.behaviour: It grazes on grass and other plants in open country.
fields.why_here: Meadows and wet areas give migrating birds places to rest.
fields.migration: It breeds in northern Eurasia and is a very rare winter visitor in France.
fields.confusions: The Greater White-fronted Goose is similar. Small size, short bill and the yellow eye ring must be judged together.
fields.hint: A thin yellow ring underlines my eye.

fields.summary: The male Spanish Sparrow has a chestnut cap, white cheeks and a lot of black on the chest and sides.
fields.behaviour: It eats seeds and catches insects, especially for its chicks.
fields.why_here: It lives in farmland and open places with trees or bushes.
fields.migration: Depending on the group, it may stay put or migrate. Movements differ around the Mediterranean.
fields.by_ear: It gives noisy chirps, especially when birds gather together.
fields.confusions: The male Italian Sparrow has sides with less black. Females are hard to identify.
fields.anecdote: It can nest in colonies and build its nests very close to its neighbours' nests.
fields.hint: My pale belly carries many black marks.

fields.summary: The male Reeves's Pheasant has a very long tail and a white head with black bars. The female has plain brown feathers.
fields.behaviour: It searches the ground for seeds, plants and small animals.
fields.why_here: It comes from China and lives in woods and along their edges. The birds in France come from introductions.
fields.migration: It mostly stays in one place and does not make a regular natural migration to France.
fields.confusions: The male Common Pheasant has a dark head and a different feather pattern.
fields.anecdote: The male's tail makes up a big part of his total length.
fields.hint: My very long tail trails behind my white head.

fields.summary: Eleonora's Falcon is a slim bird of prey with long wings, linked to Mediterranean islands and coasts. Its feathers can be pale or dark.
fields.behaviour: It catches insects in flight and hunts migrating birds to feed its young.
fields.why_here: It nests mostly on island cliffs, close to where migrating birds pass.
fields.migration: It stays in the Mediterranean in summer and spends the winter mainly in Madagascar. Some birds visit France.
fields.confusions: The Eurasian Hobby looks like it in flight, but the shape and colours need a careful look.
fields.anecdote: It breeds late to take advantage of small migrating birds passing through.
fields.hint: I raise my young when migrants cross the sea.
