fields.summary: The Aquatic Warbler is a small brown, streaky marsh bird. A pale stripe runs across the top of its head.
fields.behaviour: It catches small invertebrates, animals without a backbone, in wet plants.
fields.why_here: When it stops over, it looks for open marshes with lots of low plants.
fields.migration: It is a migrant. It crosses France between its European breeding places and its African winter homes, and is noticed mostly in late summer.
fields.confusions: The Sedge Warbler does not have the same clearly striped pattern on the top of the head and on the back.
fields.hint: A pale stripe splits the top of my head.

fields.summary: Thekla's Lark is a brown lark with a small crest, made for dry, stony ground.
fields.behaviour: It walks on the ground to pick up seeds and small invertebrates, animals without a backbone.
fields.why_here: It looks for low scrubland, dry slopes and rocky soils.
fields.migration: It mostly stays in one place, with short local moves.
fields.confusions: The Crested Lark is very similar. The shape of the bill, the streaks on the chest and the calls help tell them apart.
fields.hint: My little crest sticks up among dry stones.

fields.summary: The Collared Pratincole has long pointed wings and a forked tail. A dark border surrounds its pale throat.
fields.behaviour: It catches mostly insects in flight, with quick changes of direction.
fields.why_here: It looks for open ground near wet areas, with bare soil to nest on.
fields.migration: It is a migrant. It comes in summer and spends the winter in Africa.
fields.confusions: Its flight is like a swallow's, but its shape on the ground and its black-edged throat are very different.
fields.anecdote: It hunts in the air, while many of its relatives search for food on the ground or in the mud.

fields.summary: The Spectacled Warbler is a small bird of low scrub. The male has a grey head and a pale ring around the eye.
fields.behaviour: It looks for small insects among the twigs and leaves.
fields.why_here: It lives mostly in low plants of dry places and some coastal marshes.
fields.migration: In France, it is present mostly in summer. Mediterranean groups move in different ways.
fields.confusions: The Common Whitethroat is bigger and does not show quite the same pale pattern around the eye.

fields.summary: The Calandra Lark is a big, sturdy lark, with a thick bill and black patches on the sides of its chest.
fields.behaviour: It eats seeds and insects in open country.
fields.why_here: It looks for wide, dry plains with low plants.
fields.migration: It generally stays in one place in the south of its range, with short local moves.
fields.by_ear: Its powerful song can include copies of other birds.
fields.confusions: The Eurasian Skylark is slimmer and does not have the big black marks on the sides of its chest.
fields.anecdote: Its song can borrow sounds from birds living nearby.
fields.hint: My powerful song sometimes hides borrowed voices.

fields.summary: The Moustached Warbler is a small marsh bird with a dark head, underlined by a very clear white eyebrow.
fields.behaviour: It looks for insects and spiders in plants near water.
fields.why_here: It lives in reedbeds and thick marsh plants, mostly in Mediterranean regions.
fields.migration: Some birds stay in their region, others make seasonal moves around the Mediterranean.
fields.by_ear: Its song mixes quick sounds with rounder, flute-like notes.
fields.confusions: The Sedge Warbler has a head pattern with less contrast and a different overall look.
fields.hint: My big white eyebrow lights up a dark head.

fields.summary: The Cackling Goose is a small goose with a black head and neck, marked with a white patch on the cheek.
fields.behaviour: It grazes on grass and eats other plants in open country.
fields.why_here: Meadows and bodies of water can host the few birds seen in Europe.
fields.migration: It is a migrant from North America and is very rare in France. Some birds escaped from captivity, which makes sightings hard to read.
fields.confusions: The Canada Goose is usually bigger, with a longer neck and bill. Some forms are still hard to tell apart.
fields.hint: My white cheek stands out on my short black neck.

fields.summary: The Little Bustard is a bird of grassy plains. In breeding feathers, the male has a black neck crossed by white bars.
fields.behaviour: It eats plants and insects. Young birds especially need small prey.
fields.why_here: It looks for meadows and crops that give both food and plant cover.
fields.migration: Some French birds migrate south, while others stay in Mediterranean regions.
fields.by_ear: The male gives a short, dry call from the ground.
fields.confusions: The Great Bustard is much heavier and the male does not have this black and white pattern on the neck.
fields.anecdote: The male can leap above the plants during his display.
fields.hint: I leap in the grass with my black-and-white collar.

fields.summary: The male American Wigeon has a pale forehead and a green band behind the eye. This North American duck looks like the Eurasian Wigeon.
fields.behaviour: It likes to graze on grass and eats water plants.
fields.why_here: The few visitors use bodies of water, marshes and meadows near water.
fields.migration: It is a rare visitor to France, mostly in winter.
fields.confusions: The male Eurasian Wigeon has a reddish head, while the American Wigeon's head is greyer and greener.
fields.hint: My pale forehead sits above a green stripe by the eye.

fields.summary: The Little Bunting is a very small, streaky brown bird, with a russet and dark pattern on its cheeks.
fields.behaviour: It looks for seeds on the ground and also catches insects.
fields.why_here: When it stops over, it uses grassy and bushy places, often wet ones.
fields.migration: It breeds in northern Eurasia and spends the winter mostly in Asia. It rarely appears in France on its journeys.
fields.by_ear: Its contact call is short and dry, but it is not enough alone for a sure identification.
fields.confusions: The Common Reed Bunting is bigger. The exact head pattern matters to tell them apart.
fields.hint: My russet cheeks hide in the grass.

fields.summary: The Chiloe Wigeon is a South American duck with a head contrasting dark green and white.
fields.behaviour: It eats lots of plants and may graze on the banks.
fields.why_here: It lives on bodies of water and wet meadows. In France, it is mostly linked to bird collections and escapes from captivity.
fields.migration: Its natural migrations happen in South America. Its presence in France is not part of a regular migration route.
fields.hint: My white face stands out against a dark green head.

fields.summary: The White-winged Snowfinch is a high-mountain bird with a grey head and a pale belly. Its wings flash a lot of white in flight.
fields.behaviour: It looks for seeds and small invertebrates, animals without a backbone, on the ground, sometimes at the edge of snow patches.
fields.why_here: It lives on rocks and meadows above the treeline.
fields.migration: It stays in mountain regions, moving around depending on snow and food.
fields.confusions: The Snow Bunting can look like it in flight, but its head pattern and the place where you see it are different.
fields.anecdote: It can place its nest in cracks in rocks or in mountain buildings.
fields.hint: I live on rocks above where the forests end.

fields.summary: The Parrot Crossbill is a bird of northern forests with a big bill whose tips cross over. The male is often red, the female greenish.
fields.behaviour: It opens cones to pull out the seeds, especially those of pine trees.
fields.why_here: It looks for conifer forests that offer plenty of cones.
fields.migration: It may leave its usual areas when food runs short. It shows up in France only now and then, mostly in autumn and winter.
fields.confusions: The Red Crossbill usually has a less heavy bill. Calls and several details must be compared.
fields.anecdote: The crossed tips of its bill work like a tool to pry apart the scales of cones.

fields.summary: The Lesser Scaup is a North American diving duck. The male has a dark head, a grey back and pale sides.
fields.behaviour: It dives to look for small water animals and plants.
fields.why_here: The few visitors come to lakes, ponds and other bodies of water.
fields.migration: It is a migrant in North America and a rare visitor to France, mostly in winter.
fields.confusions: The Greater Scaup looks very much like it. The shape of the head and the wing pattern help, but must be judged carefully.
fields.hint: I dive with my dark head and pale sides.

fields.summary: The Black Guillemot is a seabird with a thin bill. In summer, its black body has a big white patch on each wing.
fields.behaviour: It dives to catch fish and small sea animals near the coast.
fields.why_here: It uses rocky shores and holes in northern coasts.
fields.migration: It often stays near the coasts of its northern range, with seasonal moves. In France, it is rare.
fields.confusions: The Common Guillemot does not have its big white wing patches or its red legs.
fields.anecdote: Its legs are bright red, and so is the inside of its mouth.
fields.hint: My feet and the inside of my mouth are bright red.

fields.summary: The Eastern Subalpine Warbler is a small bird of Mediterranean bushes. The male has a white moustache and an orange-brown tint on his belly.
fields.behaviour: It looks for small insects in the leaves and twigs.
fields.why_here: It lives in scrub and shrubby places in south-east Europe.
fields.migration: It is a migrant and spends the winter in Africa. It is rare in France.
fields.confusions: The Western Subalpine Warbler and Moltoni's Warbler are very close. To tell them apart, you must pay special attention to calls and feather details.
fields.hint: My pale moustache stands out against my russet belly.

fields.summary: The River Warbler is a small, shy brown bird of thick plants. You often find it by its non-stop song.
fields.behaviour: It catches small invertebrates, animals without a backbone, in plants and near the ground.
fields.why_here: It looks for wet areas full of tall grass and bushes.
fields.migration: It is a migrant. It spends summer in Europe and winter in Africa. It stays rare in France.
fields.by_ear: Its song is a long string of dry, steady notes, like a machine running.
fields.confusions: The Common Grasshopper Warbler sings a thinner, more continuous song, closer to an insect's.
fields.anecdote: Its name reminds us of grasshoppers, which its long strings of sounds can bring to mind.
fields.hint: My steady song sounds like a small hidden machine.

fields.summary: The Barred Warbler is a big grey warbler. Adults may show fine bars on the underside of the body.
fields.behaviour: It eats insects in bushes and also eats berries.
fields.why_here: It lives in scrub and thick hedges in open country.
fields.migration: It is a migrant and spends the winter in Africa. In France, it is mostly a rare visitor on seasonal journeys.
fields.confusions: Young birds do not have the clear bars of the adults. Their big size and the details of the wings help tell them from other warblers.
fields.hint: I hide in thick hedges and eat insects and berries.

fields.summary: The Roseate Tern is a very pale seabird with a long forked tail. Its bill is mostly dark during part of the breeding season.
fields.behaviour: It dives to catch small fish near the surface.
fields.why_here: It nests on small islands and looks for coastal waters full of fish.
fields.migration: It is a migrant. It goes to its colonies in summer and spends the winter mostly near African coasts.
fields.confusions: The Common Tern usually has a redder bill during breeding. Bill colours do change with the season, though.
fields.anecdote: It may hide its nest in a shelter under plants or between stones.
fields.hint: My long forked tail follows very pale wings.

fields.summary: The Surf Scoter is a North American sea duck. The black male has white marks on his head and a big colourful bill.
fields.behaviour: It dives to take shellfish and other small sea animals.
fields.why_here: The few visitors come mostly to coastal waters.
fields.migration: It is only very rarely seen in France, mainly in winter.
fields.confusions: The Velvet Scoter shows white in its wings. In the male Surf Scoter, the big white marks are on the head.
fields.hint: My big colourful bill stands out on a black and white head.

fields.summary: The Thrush Nightingale is a shy brown bird, very close to the Common Nightingale. It lives mostly further east and north in Europe.
fields.behaviour: It looks for small invertebrates, animals without a backbone, in dead leaves and near the ground.
fields.why_here: It likes undergrowth and thick bushes, often in wet places.
fields.migration: It is a migrant and spends the winter in Africa. It is rare in France on its journeys.
fields.by_ear: Its powerful song has repeated phrases and loud notes.
fields.confusions: The Common Nightingale is extremely similar. The voice and exact details must be added to what you see of the feathers.
fields.hint: Hidden in the bushes, I make my voice carry.

fields.summary: The Budgerigar is a small Australian bird with a long tail. The wild kind is mostly green and yellow, with black wavy patterns.
fields.behaviour: It feeds mainly on seeds and moves around in flocks.
fields.why_here: In the wild, it lives in the open spaces of Australia. In France, sightings are mostly of birds that escaped from captivity.
fields.migration: It is a nomad in its home country and follows the food. It does not migrate naturally to France.
fields.by_ear: It gives out chirps and many kinds of chatter.
fields.confusions: The Rose-ringed Parakeet is much bigger and does not have the same black waves on its feathers.
fields.anecdote: Birds bred in captivity can be blue, white or yellow, unlike the usual wild colouring.
fields.hint: Little black waves mark my feathers.

fields.summary: The White-cheeked Pintail is a brown duck with white cheeks and throat. The red base of its bill catches the eye.
fields.behaviour: It takes small animals and plants from shallow water.
fields.why_here: It naturally lives in wetlands of the Americas. Birds seen in France are usually linked to captivity.
fields.migration: It does not follow a regular natural migration route to France.
fields.hint: The red base of my bill catches the eye.

fields.summary: The Buff-breasted Sandpiper is a small bird with warm-coloured feathers and a short bill. It often walks in grass rather than in mud.
fields.behaviour: It catches small invertebrates, animals without a backbone, on open ground.
fields.why_here: During its stops, it looks for short lawns, meadows and open land.
fields.migration: It is a migrant of the Americas and rarely appears in France, mostly in autumn.
fields.confusions: The Ruff can look like it, but its shape and head details are different.
fields.anecdote: Unlike many sandpipers, it is happy to stop in fairly dry places.
fields.hint: I often prefer short grass to mud.

fields.summary: The Common Waxbill is a tiny grey-brown bird with fine stripes, a red bill and a red band around the eyes.
fields.behaviour: It picks small seeds, especially from grasses, and often feeds in a group.
fields.why_here: It comes from Africa and lives in tall grass. Introduced groups live in some parts of Europe.
fields.migration: Settled groups mostly stay in one place, with short local moves.
fields.anecdote: Its red bill looks as if it was shaped from coloured wax.
fields.hint: My red bill matches a band of the same colour.

fields.summary: The Red-billed Leiothrix is a small, lively bird with a red bill and a yellow-orange throat. It moves through thick leaves.
fields.behaviour: It eats small invertebrates, animals without a backbone, and fruit, often with other birds.
fields.why_here: It comes from Asia and settled in some parts of France after being introduced. It looks for thick undergrowth.
fields.migration: The settled groups in France mostly stay in one place, with short local moves.
fields.by_ear: Its song is made of clear, whistled and varied phrases.
fields.hint: My yellow-orange throat glows in the thick undergrowth.

fields.summary: The Lesser Yellowlegs is a North American water bird with long yellow legs and a thin, straight bill.
fields.behaviour: It catches small animals as it walks in shallow water.
fields.why_here: The few visitors look for marshes, lagoons and muddy banks.
fields.migration: It is a migrant of the Americas and rarely appears in France on its journeys.
fields.confusions: The Wood Sandpiper has a different shape and shorter legs. A careful comparison is still needed.
fields.hint: I wade in shallow water with a thin, straight bill.

fields.summary: The Lesser Grey Shrike is a grey, black and white bird. The adult has a wide black mask that spreads across the forehead.
fields.behaviour: It watches mostly for big insects from an open perch.
fields.why_here: It looks for open country with trees, wires or bushes to watch the ground from.
fields.migration: It is a migrant. It spends summer in Europe and winter in southern Africa. It has become very rare in France.
fields.confusions: The Great Grey Shrike usually has a paler forehead and a tail that is longer for its size.
fields.hint: A broad black band crosses my eyes and forehead.

fields.summary: The Helmeted Guineafowl is a round bird with dark feathers covered in little white dots. Its almost bare head has a hard bump on top.
fields.behaviour: It looks for seeds, plants and small animals as it walks on the ground, often in a group.
fields.why_here: It comes from Africa and, in France, lives mostly on farms and around them.
fields.migration: It does not migrate naturally to France. The birds here come from farms.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are loud, repeated and grating.
fields.anecdote: It likes to perch in trees to spend the night.
fields.hint: Hundreds of pale dots decorate my dark suit.

fields.summary: The Slender-billed Gull is a pale bird with a dark red bill and a fairly long neck. Its breeding feathers can have a pink tint.
fields.behaviour: It catches small animals in the water and also feeds at the surface.
fields.why_here: It lives in lagoons, salt pans and other Mediterranean coastal places.
fields.migration: It moves between coastal sites. Some birds stay in the Mediterranean while others go to regions further south.
fields.confusions: The adult Black-headed Gull has a dark head when breeding. The Slender-billed Gull keeps a pale head.
fields.hint: I keep my head pale above a long neck.

fields.summary: The adult Rosy Starling is pink and black, with a small crest. Young birds are light brown and much less colourful.
fields.behaviour: It gathers in flocks to catch insects, especially grasshoppers, and also eats fruit.
fields.why_here: It lives in open country full of food and may show up in towns or crop fields.
fields.migration: It is a migrant and sometimes arrives in France in irregular moves, mostly in summer.
fields.confusions: The adult Common Starling does not have a pink body. Young birds need a closer look.
fields.anecdote: When it turns up far from its usual home, many birds can come at once.
fields.hint: I travel in flocks and hunt grasshoppers.

fields.summary: The Mediterranean Shearwater is a seabird, dark above and white below, linked to the Mediterranean.
fields.behaviour: It catches small fish by diving and flies close to the water's surface.
fields.why_here: It nests in holes and cracks on Mediterranean islands.
fields.migration: It moves around the Mediterranean and nearby seas with the seasons. It can visit French waters all year.
fields.confusions: The Manx Shearwater and the Balearic Shearwater are close. The colour of the underside is not always enough to tell them apart.
fields.anecdote: It usually goes back to its nesting places in the dark.
fields.hint: I return to my rocky hideout at nightfall.

fields.summary: The Purple Swamphen is a big purple-blue marsh bird with a red bill and forehead. Its toes are especially long.
fields.behaviour: It eats plants and small animals, and can bring food to its bill with one foot.
fields.why_here: It looks for wetlands full of reeds and thick plants.
fields.migration: It mostly stays in one place, but can spread out to new marshes.
fields.by_ear: Its calls are loud, varied and sometimes harsh.
fields.confusions: The Common Moorhen is smaller and does not have its purple-blue feathers or its huge red bill.
fields.anecdote: Its long toes help it walk on plants and hold its food.
fields.hint: I carry my meal to my bill with one foot.

fields.summary: The Hooded Merganser is a small North American duck with a thin bill. The male spreads a big black and white crest.
fields.behaviour: It dives to catch small fish and other water animals.
fields.why_here: It lives in fresh water, often near woods, and nests in tree holes.
fields.migration: It is a migrant in North America and is very rare in France. Some of the birds seen may come from captivity.
fields.confusions: The male Smew is much whiter and does not have the same big, rounded crest.
fields.anecdote: The male's crest changes his shape a lot when he spreads it.
fields.hint: I dive for small fish and nest in tree holes.

fields.summary: Moltoni's Warbler is a small Mediterranean bird. The male has a white moustache and a belly with pinkish tones.
fields.behaviour: It looks for small insects in bushes.
fields.why_here: It lives in Mediterranean scrub, especially in Corsica.
fields.migration: It is a migrant. It comes back in summer and spends the winter in Africa.
fields.by_ear: Its call has a small rolling trill, helpful for telling it from very similar warblers.
fields.confusions: The Western Subalpine Warbler looks very much like it. The voice is often more useful than the shade of the feathers.
fields.hint: My little rolling call tells who I am in the bushes.

fields.summary: The American Golden Plover is a bird of wide open spaces with a brown back dotted with gold. Its look changes a lot between summer and winter.
fields.behaviour: It catches small invertebrates, animals without a backbone, on the ground, running and stopping in turns.
fields.why_here: The few visitors use open ground, meadows and bare banks.
fields.migration: It is a migrant of the Americas and rarely appears in France, mostly during the autumn passage.
fields.confusions: The European Golden Plover and the Pacific Golden Plover are very close. Their proportions and the underside of the wings must be checked together.
fields.hint: I run, then stop, to catch small prey on open ground.

fields.summary: The Black Wheatear is a dark bird with a white rump and a white tail for most of its length. It loves rocky, dry country.
fields.behaviour: It watches for small animals from a rock before dropping down to catch them.
fields.why_here: It lives mostly on stony ground in the Iberian Peninsula and North Africa.
fields.migration: It mostly stays in one place. Today, it is very rare in France.
fields.confusions: The Northern Wheatear does not have such an evenly dark body.
fields.anecdote: The male may carry pebbles and put them near the nesting place.
fields.hint: I sometimes carry pebbles near my nest.

fields.summary: The Cockatiel is an Australian bird with an upright crest and a long tail. The wild kind is grey, with orange cheeks.
fields.behaviour: It looks mostly for seeds on the ground and often moves in a group.
fields.why_here: It naturally lives in the open country of Australia. In France, it is mostly seen after escaping from captivity.
fields.migration: Its natural moves follow food in Australia. It does not migrate naturally to France.
fields.by_ear: It makes whistles and clear calls. Pet birds can learn whistled tunes.
fields.confusions: The Budgerigar is smaller and has no crest.
fields.anecdote: The position of its crest changes with its attention and how alert it is.
fields.hint: My movable crest sits above orange cheeks.

fields.summary: The White-backed Woodpecker is a black and white bird with white on its lower back and pink under its tail. It depends on dead trees.
fields.behaviour: It digs into damaged wood to look for insect grubs.
fields.why_here: Old forests full of dead wood give it food and trees to dig its nest in.
fields.migration: It stays in its forest regions all year round.
fields.hint: I search old damaged trunks for my meal.

fields.summary: The Barolo Shearwater is a small seabird with a dark back and a white belly. It lives mostly around Atlantic islands.
fields.behaviour: It looks for food at sea, near the surface.
fields.why_here: The open sea is its hunting ground, and its colonies are on islands.
fields.hint: Dark above, white below, I cross the waters around islands.

fields.summary: Pallas's Leaf Warbler is a tiny greenish bird with pale stripes on its head and wings. Its yellow rump shows in flight.
fields.behaviour: It checks the leaves and may hover in front of a branch to catch an insect.
fields.why_here: Trees and bushes give it insects when it stops during its journey.
fields.migration: It is an Asian migrant and may very rarely reach France, mostly in autumn.
fields.hint: My tiny back hides a yellow touch near the tail.

fields.summary: The Western Capercaillie is a big forest bird. The dark male spreads a wide, rounded tail, while the brown female blends into the undergrowth.
fields.behaviour: It eats plants, especially pine needles in winter. Males show off at gathering places.
fields.why_here: It needs quiet forests with clearings and low plants to feed on.
fields.migration: It stays in its forest areas, with short local moves.
fields.by_ear: The display mixes clicks and a rubbing sound, surprisingly quiet for such a big bird.
fields.hint: I fan out a big tail in the forest.

fields.summary: The Eurasian Three-toed Woodpecker is a black and white bird of conifer forests. The male has a yellow cap, an unusual colour among European woodpeckers.
fields.behaviour: It peels off bark to find the insects living underneath.
fields.why_here: Dead or dying conifers give it its food.
fields.migration: It usually stays in its forest regions.
fields.anecdote: Its feet have fewer toes than those of most other woodpeckers.
fields.hint: My yellow cap lights up old conifers.

fields.summary: The Red-necked Nightjar is a night bird with brown feathers that blend in very well. A reddish patch circles its neck.
fields.behaviour: It hunts insects in flight at dusk and rests quietly during the day.
fields.why_here: It lives in warm landscapes mixing open spaces and thin plant cover.
fields.migration: It is a migrant and spends the cold season in Africa. It is very rarely seen in France.

fields.summary: The White-rumped Sandpiper is a small shore bird. In flight, a white patch shows above its tail.
fields.behaviour: It pecks at small animals in the mud and shallow water.
fields.why_here: Mudflats and bare banks let it stop and feed.
fields.migration: It is a migrant of the Americas and only reaches France now and then.
fields.hint: I peck tiny animals in the mud and shallow water.

fields.summary: The Two-barred Crossbill has a bill whose tips cross over and white bars on its wings. The adult male has a red tint.
fields.behaviour: It opens conifer cones to pull out the seeds.
fields.why_here: Forests with lots of cones attract its groups.
fields.migration: Its moves follow the seed supply. It shows up in France only now and then.
fields.hint: I open conifer cones to eat the seeds.

fields.summary: The Northern Bald Ibis is a dark bird with a bare face and a long curved bill. A tuft of feathers circles the back of its head.
fields.behaviour: It probes the ground with its bill to grab small animals.
fields.why_here: It feeds in open country and uses rock walls to nest.
fields.hint: I probe the ground with my long curved bill.

fields.summary: The Rock Partridge is a chubby bird of rocky mountains. Its pale throat is edged with black and its sides have bold bars.
fields.behaviour: It walks among the stones and eats seeds, shoots and small animals.
fields.why_here: Open slopes mixing rocks and grass give it shelter and food.
fields.migration: It stays in the mountains but may change height depending on the conditions.
fields.hint: My pale throat is circled by a black line.

fields.summary: The Syrian Woodpecker is a black and white bird, very close to other woodpeckers of orchards and light woods.
fields.behaviour: It looks for insects on trees and also eats fruit and seeds.
fields.why_here: Orchards, parks and open woods suit it well.
fields.hint: I search orchard trees for my meal.

fields.summary: The Eastern Red-rumped Swallow has long wings and a forked tail. It catches its food in the air.
fields.behaviour: It snaps up small insects in mid-flight.
fields.hint: I eat my meals on the wing, my tail forked.

fields.summary: The Dusky Warbler is a small brownish bird with a pale eyebrow. It often slips through low plants.
fields.behaviour: It looks for small insects among the leaves and twigs.
fields.why_here: Thick bushes, especially near water, give it shelter when it stops during its journey.
fields.migration: It is an Asian migrant and rarely reaches France, mostly in autumn.
fields.hint: My pale eyebrow slips through the bushes.

fields.summary: The Broad-billed Sandpiper is a small mudflat bird with a bill that bends slightly downward. Its face shows pale lines.
fields.behaviour: It looks for small animals in wet mud.
fields.why_here: The edges of lagoons and mudflats give it places to stop and feed.
fields.migration: It crosses Europe during migration. It is not often seen passing through France.
fields.hint: My slightly curved bill explores the mud.

fields.summary: The White-headed Duck is a chubby duck that often cocks its stiff tail. The breeding male has a white head and a big blue bill.
fields.behaviour: It dives to look for food under the water.
fields.why_here: Bodies of water edged with plants give it food and shelter.
fields.hint: My tail stands up above the water like a little mast.

fields.summary: The Black-bellied Sandgrouse is a bird of dry plains. Its black belly contrasts with earth-coloured feathers above.
fields.behaviour: It picks up mostly seeds on the ground and flies to water holes to drink.
fields.why_here: Wide, dry, open ground suits it well.
fields.hint: I pick seeds on dry plains and fly to water to drink.

fields.summary: The Pin-tailed Sandgrouse is a bird of dry plains with a white belly and a pointed tail. Its colours camouflage it on the ground.
fields.behaviour: It looks for seeds on the ground and may fly to water in a group.
fields.why_here: Dry stretches with low plants give it space to feed.
fields.migration: It is present all year in its home areas, moving to find water and food.
fields.anecdote: The male carries water in the feathers of his belly to give his chicks a drink.
fields.hint: I carry water in my belly feathers for my chicks.

fields.summary: The Iberian Magpie has a black cap, a pale body and a long bluish tail. It is a sociable bird of the Iberian Peninsula.
fields.behaviour: It feeds in a group, taking insects, fruit and seeds.
fields.why_here: Open woods and landscapes with scattered trees suit it well.
fields.hint: My long blue tail goes along on my outings with the gang.

fields.summary: The Mediterranean Short-toed Lark is a small brown bird of open country. Its plain feathers blend in with the soil.
fields.behaviour: It looks for seeds and small insects on the ground.
fields.why_here: Open ground with low plants lets it move around and feed.
fields.hint: My earth-coloured feathers hide me on the ground.

fields.summary: Ross's Goose is a small North American goose. Its white form shows black wingtips and a short bill.
fields.behaviour: It grazes on plants, often with other geese.
fields.why_here: Open meadows and bodies of water give it food and rest.
fields.hint: All white, I show black at the wingtips.

fields.summary: The Eastern Black-eared Wheatear is a small bird of stony ground. The breeding male shows black wings contrasting with a pale body.
fields.behaviour: It watches for insects from a low perch, then drops down to catch them.
fields.why_here: Open, rocky country gives it lookout posts.
fields.migration: It is a migrant and spends the cold season in Africa. It turns up in France only now and then.
fields.hint: From rock to rock, I watch for insects.

fields.summary: The Lesser Spotted Eagle is a brown bird of prey with broad wings. It lives in landscapes mixing forests and open spaces.
fields.behaviour: It looks for small animals, sometimes walking in the meadows.
fields.why_here: Forests give it nest sites and open places give it hunting grounds.
fields.migration: It is a migrant and spends the winter in Africa. It is rare in France.
fields.hint: I may hunt on foot in meadows.

fields.summary: The Long-billed Dowitcher is a wetland bird with a long, straight bill. It probes the mud with repeated moves.
fields.behaviour: It pushes its bill into soft ground to look for small animals.
fields.why_here: Marshes and shallow muddy banks give it food.
fields.migration: Its usual routes pass mostly through the Americas. It appears in France only now and then.
fields.hint: I jab the soft mud again and again.

fields.summary: The Rock Ptarmigan is a high-mountain bird whose feathers change with the seasons. White in winter, it becomes a mix of brown and grey.
fields.behaviour: It feeds mostly on plants and walks among the rocks.
fields.why_here: Cold landscapes above the treeline give it places to feed and hide.
fields.migration: It stays in the mountains, with short local moves depending on the conditions.
fields.confusions: The Willow Ptarmigan lives mostly in northern regions. The male Rock Ptarmigan has a black line between the eye and the bill, visible on his white head in winter.
fields.hint: I change my camouflage when the mountain turns white.

fields.summary: Dupont's Lark is a streaky brown bird with a thin, curved bill. Shy, it moves between small clumps of plants.
fields.behaviour: It walks on the ground looking for food.
fields.why_here: Wide, dry stretches with low plants are its home.
fields.hint: My curved bill sticks out of the low grass.

fields.summary: The Eastern Olivaceous Warbler is a small bird with plain feathers, grey-brown above and pale below.
fields.behaviour: It looks for insects in the branches and leaves.
fields.why_here: Bushes and light woods give it food and shelter.
fields.hint: Quiet and pale, I look for my meal among leaves.

fields.summary: The Spanish Imperial Eagle is a large bird of prey of the Iberian Peninsula. The dark adult has clear white patches on its shoulders.
fields.behaviour: It hunts rabbits in open country, among other prey.
fields.why_here: Landscapes mixing big trees and open hunting grounds suit it well.
fields.hint: My white shoulders light up my dark outline.

fields.summary: The Golden Pheasant is an Asian bird raised in parks. The male has a yellow crest, a long tail and a red belly.
fields.behaviour: It looks for seeds, plants and small animals on the ground.
fields.why_here: Thick plants let it hide. A bird seen in France may come from captivity.
fields.hint: My yellow crest tops a red suit and a long tail.

fields.summary: The Emperor Goose is a goose of the North Pacific with a finely patterned grey body. The adult has a white head and a pale nape.
fields.behaviour: It takes plants and small animals, especially on the coast.
fields.why_here: Coastal places are an important part of its natural home.
fields.hint: My white head contrasts with my finely patterned grey coat.

fields.summary: The King Eider is a sea duck of the far north. The breeding male has an amazing orange bump above his bill.
fields.behaviour: It dives to catch animals that live in the sea.
fields.why_here: Coastal waters give it places to feed.
fields.migration: It leaves its Arctic breeding places to spend the winter at sea. It is only very rarely seen in France.
fields.hint: A funny orange bump sits above my bill.

fields.summary: The Willow Ptarmigan is a bird of cold northern regions. Its feathers can turn white in winter, depending on the group.
fields.behaviour: It eats mostly plants, especially buds and twigs.
fields.why_here: The tundra and heaths give it low plants to feed on.
fields.hint: I peck at buds in the far north.

fields.summary: Hume's Leaf Warbler is a small grey-green bird with a pale eyebrow and pale marks on its wings.
fields.behaviour: It catches small insects as it explores the branches.
fields.why_here: Trees and bushes give it food when it stops during its journey.
fields.migration: It is an Asian migrant and may very rarely spend the cold season in France.
fields.hint: My pale eyebrow underlines a tiny face in the branches.

fields.summary: Bonaparte's Gull is a small North American gull. The adult has a dark hood in the breeding season and a thin black bill.
fields.behaviour: It takes small fish and invertebrates, animals without a backbone, in the water or in flight.
fields.why_here: Lakes, rivers and coasts give it places to feed.
fields.migration: It migrates in North America. A few birds reach Europe, especially in the cold season.
fields.anecdote: It may build its nest in a conifer, a surprising habit for a bird you imagine mostly by the water.
fields.hint: Small and light, I fish with my thin black bill.

fields.summary: The breeding male Black-headed Bunting combines a black head, a yellow belly and a russet-brown back. The female is plainer.
fields.behaviour: It eats seeds and also catches insects.
fields.why_here: Open country with bushes gives it food and perches.
fields.migration: It is a migrant and normally spends the winter in southern Asia. It turns up in France now and then in summer.
fields.hint: In spring, my belly is bright yellow and my back russet.

fields.summary: Marmora's Warbler is a small grey bird with a long tail, linked to Mediterranean landscapes. It likes to stay hidden in low plants.
fields.behaviour: It looks for small insects in bushes.
fields.why_here: Heaths and low scrub give it shelter and food.
fields.hint: My long tail slips between Mediterranean bushes.

fields.summary: The Rufous-tailed Scrub Robin is a sand-coloured bird with a long reddish tail, ending in black and white. It often raises this very visible tail.
fields.behaviour: It looks mostly for small animals on the ground.
fields.why_here: Warm, open country with bushes gives it food and shelter.
fields.migration: It is a migrant and spends the winter in Africa. It is very rarely seen in France.
fields.hint: I wear sandy colours and often cock my long tail.

fields.summary: The Hazel Grouse is a forest bird with feathers mixing brown, grey and russet. It easily hides in the undergrowth.
fields.behaviour: It eats buds, leaves, fruit and small animals, depending on the season.
fields.why_here: Forests with varied undergrowth give it food and hiding places.
fields.migration: It stays in its forest areas all year round.
fields.by_ear: Its song is a very thin, high whistle, easy to miss.
fields.hint: My thin whistle drifts from undergrowth where I hide.

fields.summary: The Blue-winged Teal is a small American duck. The breeding male has a white crescent in front of the eye, and a blue patch shows on the wing.
fields.behaviour: It looks for seeds and small animals in shallow water.
fields.why_here: Marshes and shallow bodies of water give it places to feed.
fields.migration: It migrates in the Americas and may reach France by accident during its journeys.

fields.summary: The Sociable Lapwing is a bird of the plains. In flight, its wings show a bold black and white pattern.
fields.behaviour: It looks for small animals as it walks on the ground.
fields.why_here: Open ground with little cover lets it feed.
fields.migration: It migrates between its breeding areas in Central Asia and its winter homes. It is very rarely seen in France.
fields.hint: My open wings show black and white.

fields.summary: The Laughing Dove is a bird with pink and brown tones. A patch spotted with black decorates the front of its neck.
fields.behaviour: It pecks mostly at seeds on the ground.
fields.why_here: Gardens, crop fields and open places with trees suit it well.
fields.hint: A small black pattern decorates my pink neck.

fields.summary: The Maned Duck is an Australian bird that spends a lot of time on land. The male has a brown head and a small mane.
fields.behaviour: It grazes in grassy places, often in a group.
fields.why_here: Meadows near water suit it well. Birds seen in France may come from captivity.
fields.anecdote: It may nest in a tree hole even though it feeds mainly on land.
fields.hint: I often prefer grazing on grass to swimming.

fields.summary: The Yellow-crowned Bishop is a small African bird. The breeding male turns yellow and black, while the female keeps streaky brown feathers.
fields.behaviour: It eats seeds and also small insects.
fields.why_here: Tall grass and wet areas are part of its home.
fields.hint: I live in tall grass and wet areas, and eat seeds.

fields.summary: The Chilean Flamingo is a big pink bird of South America. Its greyish legs have clear pink joints.
fields.behaviour: It strains the water with its bill to catch tiny living things.
fields.why_here: Lagoons and shallow lakes give it places to feed. In France, a sighting may be a bird that came from captivity.
fields.hint: My grey legs have clear pink touches.
